The margin and finance-cost gains are already in the reported Q3FY21 results, which is a disqualifier under the fatal-flaw rule. No deep research.

label: POWERGRID
legal_name: Power Grid Corporation of India Limited
rationale: The trigger is a Letter of Intent to a successful TBCB bidder, which is not firm, and the packet gives no value or quantity to size against TTM revenue (38,499.70 cr). It is one of two similar transmission-bid LoIs within four days, so it is routine flow rather than a change. REJECT as routine and not firm.

label: EKC
rationale: The 2,00,000-cylinder capacity is a board-approved plan phased to FY2023-24 with no commissioning, so not firm. Sized at 50% year-one utilisation and an assumed Rs 5,000 per cylinder it is about Rs 50 cr, or 5.8% of trailing revenue of Rs 863.5 cr, below threshold. The hydrogen demand is conditional on trials and unquantified, so the case is watch-only until a firm hydrogen order or phase-1 start appears; the margin gain itself is unexplained.

label: GRASIM
rationale: The largest new-capacity item, UltraTech's 12.8 MTPA expansion, is board-approved and not firm. At 50% year-one utilisation and an assumed INR 3,500 per tonne it is about INR 2,240 crore, roughly 3% of TTM revenue of INR 72,909 crore, so it is immaterial to group earnings and is routine cement capacity planning. The debt reduction and margin and profit gains are already in reported Q3FY21 results with no new operating mechanism, so there is no deep research case.

label: PREMEXPLN
rationale: The two MoD orders are stated and firm: Rs 20.33 cr (flares) and Rs 13.78 cr (chaffs), together 22.2% of TTM revenue of Rs 153.71 cr (flares alone 13.2%). They are the first order disclosures on record and the PSOM-XL space qualification is a new product line, so the literal test is not routine, though defence revenue already runs at about Rs 26 cr a quarter and that must be tested. Loss-making status and undisclosed debt are unresolved but do not establish the stressed disqualifier on this packet.

label: RITES
rationale: The largest firm order is the KIIFB PMC award of INR 61.25 crore, about 3.4% of TTM revenue of INR 1,794 crore. RITES says it won more than 60 projects in Q3FY21, so these orders are routine flow rather than an inflection. The Haryana order is only L-1 and not firm, and the reported margin gain has no operating mechanism in the packet.

label: GODREJCP
rationale: The change is a lower finance cost from routine debt repayment, which is a balance-sheet effect rather than an operating change. Annualising the Rs 23.7 cr quarterly drop gives roughly 0.9% of trailing revenue (Rs 10,452 cr), which is immaterial. The pricing move is routine. Reject: financial change with no operating explanation and immaterial.

label: GAYAPROJ
rationale: The L-1 bid of INR 1,323.52 cr is 38.4% of TTM revenue of INR 3,450.58 cr, but it is not firm (L-1 only). Order flow is routine: the company's own Q3FY21 presentation reports INR 2,144 cr and INR 1,324 cr of orders won since Q3FY21, roughly a year's revenue in a few months. The company is also under a lender debt resolution plan with a moratorium, so the STRESSED disqualifier applies; the debt reduction is non-operating claim monetisation.

label: VARROC
rationale: The EUR 41 million of re-wins is roughly INR 361 crore at an assumed INR 88 per EUR, about 3.5 percent of trailing revenue of INR 10,428 crore, and re-wins are routine for a tier-I auto component group. The fall in net debt to INR 2,730 crore is balance-sheet repair from cash flow, not a change in earnings. Heavy trailing losses (PAT -INR 621 crore) alongside high net debt meet the stressed-company disqualifier.

label: GENUSPOWER
rationale: Size: 10,000 gas meters x assumed Rs 2,000 per meter = Rs 2 crore, 0.3% of TTM revenue of Rs 665.46 crore (estimated from quantity). It is firm (order received), and gas metering is a new product line, so it is not routine. Management's market view (Rs 800-1,000 crore industry, at least 15% share, transcript page 5) would put the path above 10% of TTM revenue, but it is unfirm, so the milestone is conversion of the next order rather than deep research now.

label: SOLARINDS
rationale: Size is unknown: the order has no stated value and the three plants have no capacity quantity (the transcript says the project details are yet to be finalised), so the INR 210 crore and 180 crore capex figures cannot size revenue. Nothing is firm yet: the board has only approved a plan, and the order awaits bulk-production clearance, so it is conditional. The company is profitable (TTM PAT INR 246 crore) and the defence order is company-specific, so it goes on watch with clearance, first supply and disclosed plant capacity as the milestones.

label: GREENLAM
rationale: The product launches are unquantified and are line extensions within a Rs 1,108 cr trailing revenue base, which makes them routine rather than a new revenue stream. The margin gain and finance cost drop have no identified operating event, and the finance cost change is a financial item. Size is unknown and no disqualifier is needed to reject.

label: SOUTHWEST
rationale: The Rs 1 crore GSI letter of award is firm but about 1% of TTM revenue of Rs 102.7 crore, which is immaterial against the 10% test. It is a single small exploration job, so it cannot explain the Q3 revenue and profit jump, which remains unexplained by any event in the packet. The illiquid, sub-Rs 140 crore company gives no path to material earnings change from this award.

label: PRAJIND
rationale: The stated INR 226.90 cr binding order is 21.9 percent of trailing four-quarter revenue of INR 1,033.86 cr, above the 10 percent threshold. It is firm: a received order from an external customer, IOCL. No comparable earlier order is in the packet, so it is treated as non-routine on this evidence. No disqualifier applies; the company is profitable with negligible finance cost. The order postdates the Q3 quarter, so it cannot explain the Q3 margin gain; execution timing and order margin remain open.

label: MATRIMONY
rationale: The only trigger is a generic 'launched new products and services' line in the Q3 release, with no named product, customer or value, so there is nothing to size (TTM revenue 370.86 cr; size unknown). The margin and profit gains are in the Q3 results filed the same day, so they are already in reported results and the packet gives no operating cause. This is boilerplate rather than a specific change: FATAL_FLAW, no deep research.

label: THERMAX
rationale: Size estimated at about 0.13%: two boilers at an assumed INR 3 crore each give INR 6 crore against TTM revenue of 4,539.69 crore; the other items are unquantified. Boiler and energy-plant orders are the company's normal flow at this revenue base, and the 33 MW synchronisation is not a new revenue event in the packet. The margin gain is not tied to a specific order, so there is no inflection.

label: RAMCOCEM
rationale: Size: 1 MTPA grinding x 50% year-one utilisation x Rs 4,500/t = Rs 225 crore, 4.5% of TTM revenue of Rs 5,051.27 crore (about 9% at full run-rate), estimated from quantity. It is not firm: the Kurnool unit is a funded plan and not commissioned. The reported margin rise is mainly fuel and power cost, not capacity, so it does not yet qualify as an operating inflection. Watch Kurnool commissioning and disclosed volumes.

label: MOTHERSON
rationale: Size is unknown: no value is stated for the debt reduction, and the trigger is a balance-sheet event rather than an order or product. The profit rise is a financial change whose only disclosed driver is lower gross debt and finance cost; no operating mechanism is shown, and the Q3 FY20 base was pre-COVID so no low-base effect explains it. No firm order or new product exists. Rejected under the no-operating-explanation rule.

label: TCIFINANCE
rationale: A loan was repaid and pledged shares released, which is firm, but the company is a microcap (market cap about INR 8 cr) and its finance cost fell by about INR 0.5 cr a quarter with no operating event. Operating profit growth from INR 0.91 cr to 1.46 cr has no identified mechanism and the revenue jump is unexplained. The change is immaterial on the packet evidence and does not meet the earnings-inflection test.

label: CUPID
rationale: WHO/UNFPA pre-qualification is company-specific and could open UN and public-sector procurement, but it is eligibility to bid, not an order or a regulatory approval, so it is not firm. The packet gives no volumes, prices or tender values, so size against TTM revenue (141.63 cr) is unknown. Revenue has been falling, so the path to a material contribution is unproven; watch for the first UN-agency or public purchase order.

label: IGPL
rationale: Size: PA-4 53,000 TPA x 50% first-year utilisation = 26,500 t, x Rs 60/kg (assumed low end) = Rs 159 crore, or 16.4% of TTM revenue of Rs 967.73 crore. Commissioning on 29 Dec 2020 is firm and most of its output is not yet in reported results. It adds about 24% to existing capacity, a step-change on the packet evidence, so not routine; the 80,000 TPA greenfield (about Rs 600 crore, about three years) is a plan and is not sized. Deep research should test PA-4 utilisation and realisation and the greenfield funding.

label: SATIA
rationale: 12,000 t at the company-stated average realisation of Rs 55,000/t gives Rs 66.0 cr, or 11.1% of trailing revenue of Rs 594.70 cr (the lower-realisation case; the Rs 33 cr stated for the 5,000 t Chhattisgarh order would take the total to about 12%). The orders are awarded, so firm; the packet shows no earlier comparable order and the company presents institutional sales as a recent push, so not routine. Trailing PAT is positive at Rs 44.72 cr with low finance cost, so no stress disqualifier; the realisation gain is the main margin driver.

label: JUBLFOOD
rationale: A new brand in an existing biryani segment is a line extension within an existing segment and is routine, not a new revenue stream of the scale needed for the 10% test. Its revenue is not stated and the packet has no size measure, so it is immaterial on the evidence. The margin gain is attributed only to the launch with no disclosed mechanism, and no disqualifier is needed to reject.

label: INE624C01015
rationale: The packet's commercial-start event is station 1's 2015 PCOD, which is not a new change. Station 2 is the only forward item: it is not firm (a 'likely' completion by March 2021 after prior delays) and has no quantity or financials, so size is unknown. Watch for station 2 PCOD and its first revenue, and confirm the stock still trades before any research.

label: AUROPHARMA
rationale: Thirteen ANDA approvals and eleven launches in a quarter are routine flow for a generic company with TTM revenue of Rs 24,931.56 crore, and the packet shows no earlier comparable disclosures to make them a step change. The 310 bps gross-margin rise and the 47.5% finance-cost fall have no operating mechanism identified in the packet, and the Rs 2,813.89 crore exceptional item sits outside operating profit. This is a financial change with no operating explanation, so reject.

label: DCAL
rationale: Size is unknown: the business update gives no value, volume or customer for the first commercial ADC campaign and no product quantity. It is company-specific and a step from validation toward commercial supply, so not routine, but no supply agreement or PO is disclosed, so not firm. Revenue fell 13.6% YoY in the December quarter and the margin driver is unexplained, so it goes on watch until a committed value appears.

label: CYIENT
rationale: Size is unknown because no investment amount, customer order or revenue is stated, against TTM revenue of INR 4,113 cr. The event is a customer-qualification and platform announcement with no firm order, and it is a product-level investment in an existing aerospace digitisation business rather than a change in trajectory. There is no plausible path to 10% of revenue from the packet alone, so it is rejected as immaterial, with LOW confidence.

label: PIONEEREMB
rationale: Size is unknown: the borrowing reduction is unquantified, and TTM revenue is Rs 198 cr. The profit gain is mainly the interest-cost effect of lower borrowings, a financial change, and the margin move has no identified operating event. Reject as a financial change with no operating explanation.

label: HAL
rationale: The packet's trigger events are MoUs and an LoI with no value or quantity, so they are not firm and their size against TTM revenue (21,286 cr) is unknown. The read releases add a firm five-year GE forgings contract worth over INR 100 cr (about 0.5 percent of TTM revenue, immaterial) and a firm Rolls-Royce forging award with no stated value, which keeps this on watch. The IAF HTT-40 RFP for 70 aircraft is a large potential programme but is not yet a contract. No disqualifier applies; HAL is profitable.

label: TARIL
rationale: Orders from a state utility and EPC contractors are the ordinary product flow for a transformer and rectifier maker, and the packet states no order value or quantity, so size against TTM revenue of INR 621 crore is unknown. The margin gain has no operating explanation beyond these routine orders, and TTM PAT is still slightly negative. Rejected as routine flow; LOW confidence because the packet has no earlier order history to test against.

label: ALPHAGEO
rationale: Size: the award letter states Rs 77 crore (inclusive of taxes), 60.6% of TTM revenue of Rs 127.06 crore; the tax-exclusive share would be lower. It is firm (letter of award received). Routine status cannot be established: the packet has no earlier order disclosures and the company had a Rs 134 crore quarter in Jun-2019, so a Rs 77 crore seismic contract may be normal project flow resuming after the COVID stoppage. It goes on watch until order history or the execution schedule shows the award is outside normal flow.

label: NLCINDIA
rationale: Size: 500 MW x 8,760 h x 60% thermal load factor = 2.628 billion kWh, x Rs 2.50/kWh (assumed low end of usual Indian thermal tariffs) = Rs 657 crore, or 6.5% of TTM revenue of Rs 10,075.87 crore. Commercial operation declared on 10 Feb 2021 is firm and not in reported results, and a new 500 MW unit is a step beyond routine flow, but the estimate is below the 10% bar, so WATCH with a path to material if tariff or load runs above assumption.

label: VSSL
rationale: The only changes shown are financial and margin movements (operating profit up 564.1% YoY, finance cost down), with no commercial event, order, capacity or trigger passage identified in the packet, so no event value or firmness can be established. Revenue growth may reflect reclassification, and the item has been waiting 185 days without a catalyst. Rejected as a financial change with no operating explanation.

label: INE890A01016
rationale: JMC's own YTD FY21 order inflow of Rs 7,484 crore is about 175% of annualised Q3 revenue of Rs 4,264 crore (Rs 1,066 crore x 4), so order booking is routine for an EPC contractor with a Rs 14,203 crore book. The packet's Rs 13,744 crore headline is group-level, and the Rs 612 crore debt figure belongs to the parent, so the trigger is misattributed. The debt reduction is attributed to collections and working capital, which is not an inflection.

label: RML
rationale: The three firm orders total INR 86 crore a year, about 7.5 percent of trailing revenue of INR 1,141 crore, with each line 2.3 to 2.8 percent. That is below the 10 percent threshold, and they fall within the group's ordinary auto component product lines with no step-change shown. The loss-making trailing results and the preferential equity raise do not change the size result, so it is rejected as immaterial and routine.

label: HIMATSEIDE
rationale: The Rs 285 crore is a net-debt reduction, a balance-sheet and financial change that rule 1 does not use to size an event, and it brings no revenue. No operating event separate from the debt cut qualifies: the margin rise has no commercial event in the packet, and the Rs 200-400 crore a year is non-binding deleveraging guidance. Re-triage if the capex completion is shown to add revenue-generating capacity.

label: SHREEPUSHK
rationale: The DI expansion (about 22,000 TPA, Rs 75 cr capex about 85% spent, guided Q1FY22) is company-specific new capacity, but it is a plan, not firm. Using 22,000 TPA x 50% utilisation x an assumed low-end Rs 1 lakh/t gives Rs 110 cr, about 34% of TTM revenue of Rs 322.96 cr, as an upper bound because the incremental share is not disclosed. The Jhabua shipments are already in reported results and do not qualify on their own, so the case is WATCH until commercial production is reported.

label: TTKPRESTIG
rationale: Adding 25 SKUs is routine product management for a consumer-products company, and no value or volume is stated, so size is unknown. The margin and profit gain is not tied to any discrete, non-routine event in the packet. Reject as routine flow with no operating explanation beyond ordinary SKU additions.

label: KRBL
rationale: The stated Rs 418 cr net debt reduction is 10.2% of trailing revenue (Rs 4,080 cr), but it is a balance-sheet item whose interest effect is already in the reported Dec-2020 quarter (finance cost down 67%). That makes it a fatal flaw (already fully in reported results). The chia and flax launch is unquantified and was previously intimated in 2018, so it is not a new change.

label: GREENPLY
rationale: The finance cost decline comes from working capital and debt management, and the margin and profit improvement is attributed to a cyclical recovery towards pre-COVID demand, which is a low-base effect. No discrete, non-routine event or quantified value appears in the packet. Reject as a financial change with no operating explanation beyond recovery.

label: GRAVITA
rationale: The annual agreement is signed and stated at about INR 180 cr, or 13.3% of TTM revenue of INR 1,350.70 cr, so it is firm and the size is stated. It is a commodity lead supply contract in the company's existing recycling business, which is the normal flow for this company, and the packet does not show it to be a new customer, product or market, so it is judged routine. It is REJECT_WITH_REASON at low confidence; the margin rise is not explained by it, and a disclosure of new-customer status would reopen the case.

label: HITECH
rationale: The Khopoli plant has commenced commercial production, so it is firm capacity. At an estimated INR 220 cr (80,000 t x 50% year-one utilisation x assumed INR 55,000 per tonne), it is about 17.6% of trailing revenue of INR 1,248.91 cr. A plant adding about 16% to installed capacity, into a new Western region, is clearly bigger than anything the packet shows the company disclosing before; output started after the Dec-2020 quarter, so it is not already in results, and the group-ownership flag is a structure question, not a disqualifier.

label: M&M
rationale: Periodic price increases are routine for a vehicle maker with Rs 81,696 crore of TTM revenue, and the increase took effect after the quarter in which the segment turned profitable, so it cannot explain that swing. The segment result is already in reported results, and the packet gives no quantified incremental effect. Reject as routine pricing with no quantified change; trailing PAT is a loss of Rs 1,391.63 crore.

label: KPIL
rationale: Size: the Rs 13,744 crore is a nine-month cumulative order inflow, about 111% of trailing revenue of Rs 12,390 crore, and the debt reduction is balance-sheet only. The orders are received, but the flow is routine: an EPC and transmission company whose order inflow runs above annual revenue within nine months is not showing a step change, and the Rs 3,850 crore L1 is not firm. The gross margin gain is not tied to any order in the packet. Rejected as routine order flow and an unexplained financial change.

label: ARMANFIN
rationale: The item is a debt-cost reduction: finance cost of 17.2 crore is about 8.5% of TTM revenue of 201.85 crore, and it comes from lower borrowing rates and repayment, which is a financial change with no operating explanation. The packet shows revenue and PAT falling year on year, and the margin and finance-cost checks could not be verified. Rejected.

label: DHAMPURSUG
rationale: The INR 26.5 crore debt repayment is 0.62 percent of TTM revenue of INR 4,251 crore, and its only effect is a lower finance cost. The 37 percent drop in finance cost and the 35 to 38 percent revenue growth have no operating explanation beyond the debt repayment and COVID-period recovery, so this is a financial change rather than an earnings inflection. No disqualifier is needed; the rejection is on materiality and lack of a new operating driver.

label: TATASTEEL
rationale: The 9MFY21 net debt reduction of INR 18,609 cr is firm and about 13.8% of TTM revenue of INR 134,807 cr, but it is a balance-sheet change funded from cash flow whose earnings effect runs through finance cost (down about INR 153 cr YoY in Q3). The 161% operating profit jump is measured from a weak Q3FY20 base, and the packet names no company-specific operating event beyond a steel-cycle recovery, so it is a low-base and cyclical change, not a trajectory shift. No stress disqualifier applies because deleveraging is itself the fix.

label: TDPOWERSYS
rationale: The price increases are real but unquantified, and the margin step-up to 14.3% in the Dec 2020 quarter and the Sep 2020 quarter are already in reported results, so the benefit is largely in the reported numbers. The packet has no quantified incremental effect and no order, so size is unknown against trailing revenue of Rs 576.60 crore. It is treated as already in reported results (fatal flaw) and rejected, with the next reported quarter as the check.

label: CONTROLPR
rationale: Size is unknown: the order values are not disclosed and the packet gives no quantity. The tender wins are firm as received orders, but tender wins in an existing segment are ordinary business, so they are routine. The FMCG inroads and product launch are management statements without values, and reported growth is ordinary, so reject.

label: RAJESHEXPO
rationale: Firm INR 1,352 crore export order equals about 0.7% of trailing-four-quarter consolidated revenue of INR 195,600 crore. The company describes it as a resumption of normal export flow after the pandemic, a recovery effect rather than a step-change. Immaterial at this scale, with no disqualifier; no deep research warranted.

label: JUBLPHARMA
rationale: The Rs570 crore net debt reduction is about 6.8% of trailing revenue of Rs8,430.56 crore, below the 10% threshold. It is a financial change, and the gross margin and finance-cost gains have no identified operating mechanism in the packet, with discontinued operations complicating comparability. Rejected as a financial change without an operating explanation.

label: ARVIND
rationale: The Rs197 crore net borrowing reduction is about 3.9% of trailing-four-quarter revenue of Rs5,059.67 crore, well below the 10% threshold, and is a financial change. The pricing action is unquantified and described alongside continued margin pressure, so it is ordinary pricing rather than a step-change. Rejected as immaterial and without a clear operating inflection.

label: ADANIGREEN
rationale: Size is estimated from quantity: 600 MW x 8,760 h x 35 percent hybrid plant load factor (the electricity rule, which replaces the 50 percent new-capacity utilisation) x INR 2.41/kWh stated tariff = about INR 443 cr, or 15.6 percent of TTM revenue of INR 2,834.81 cr. The LoA is firm and, against a packet history whose largest item is a 150 MW commissioning, a 600 MW award is a step-change rather than routine flow. No disqualifier applies: leverage is very high, but TTM PAT is positive and recent equity financing is recorded, so STRESSED is not applied; funding and PPA terms are left for research.

label: GPTINFRA
rationale: The Rs 8.2 bn of year-to-date orders equals about 141% of TTM revenue of INR 582 cr, and the packet's Rs 2 bn L1 bid equals about 34%, but the company wins eight-plus orders of this kind in a period and a Rs 64 cr order was booked in January, so this is its normal order flow for a construction company. The packet records the amounts as non-binding, which is not firm, and the L1 is not firm either. Routine flow means REJECT_WITH_REASON, and no other disqualifier was assessed.

label: RAMCOSYS
rationale: The closed European aviation deal is firm and marks entry into a new region, so it is plausibly not routine, though the company also reports several other $3M+ deals each quarter. Size against revenue is unknown because the deal value is not disclosed and the quarter's USD 38 million booking is multi-year and spans several business lines (TTM revenue about Rs 609 crore). The company is debt-light after repaying about Rs 84 crore, with no disqualifier. Watch for the deal value and its revenue-recognition timing in the Q4 filing before any deep research.

label: ASHIANA
rationale: The NCD redemptions total about Rs 7.2 crore against trailing revenue of Rs 245.95 crore (about 2.9%), and they are scheduled and routine. The margin and PAT improvement has no operating explanation: revenue was down 35.1% in Q2 and down 0.7% in Q3 FY21, and the Q3 PAT is driven by other income of Rs 16.38 crore. That is a financial change with no operating mechanism, so reject.

label: MMP
rationale: Commercial operation from 1 Feb 2021 is firm, but the update says customers are only on trial lots and nominal revenue is expected in Q4, so near-term revenue is immaterial. No quantity is given, so size is unknown against FY20 revenue of Rs 241.82 crore; whether foil is a new stream or an extension of an existing foil business is not established. Watch for Q4 foil revenue and volumes.

label: TORNTPOWER
rationale: The 362 MW coal supply is an L1 (lowest bidder) position with the LoA awaited and the matter sub-judice, so it is not firm. Estimated size is about 4.6% of TTM revenue (300 MW x 60% load factor x Rs 3.50/kWh assumed low-end tariff = Rs 552 cr, Rs 12,072 cr TTM); it stays below 10% on any tariff up to about Rs 7.6/kWh. The Rs 8,800 cr capex is an investment amount, not revenue. It is credible and company-specific, so WATCH until a letter of award is received.

label: CAPACITE
rationale: The INR 148.2 crore Raymond order is firm and equals about 18.1% of TTM revenue of INR 818 crore. It is a repeat order from an existing client, and nothing in the packet shows a new product, customer or market, so it is routine construction flow. The Q3 revenue rebound is largely a COVID-recovery low-base effect, and the trailing loss persists, so no deep research.

label: GODREJAGRO
rationale: The only operating event is a product launch and relaunch that the packet does not size, and it is an incremental line within a Rs 6,432 cr trailing revenue base, so it is routine. The 538 bps gross margin gain has no identified operating explanation, and the finance cost drop is attributed to unexplained debt reduction, which is a financial change. Size is unknown and no disqualifier applies.

label: SWSOLAR
legal_name: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Limited
rationale: The signed Kom Ombo order of about Rs 930 cr is 16.1% of trailing revenue of Rs 5,776.89 cr and is firm, so size and firmness pass. The board disclosure says the group faces challenges obtaining funding for timely repayment of borrowings, which makes it a stressed company unlikely to capture the benefit, and the order is not the fix. Disqualified as STRESSED; reject.

label: RTSPOWR
rationale: Commercial production at a new wholly owned subsidiary is firm and adds a new revenue line, so it is not routine. Size against revenue is unknown because the packet has no financial snapshot and no value or quantity for the output. The start falls within the quarter already reported, so part of the benefit may already be in results. Watch for a disclosed subsidiary revenue contribution before any deep research.

label: WABAG
rationale: The Biel (EUR 26 mn) and Tunisia (EUR 11 mn) orders are received, so firm; together EUR 37 mn is about 12.4% of trailing revenue Rs 2,620 cr at an assumed Rs 88 per EUR, and the signed Libya contract (EUR 62 mn, activated on L/C) takes the stated total to about a third. The release calls the Swiss order the subsidiary's biggest ever and the Libya order the largest thermal desalination order in company history, and the packet shows no comparable order, so not routine. No disqualifier: trailing PAT is positive at Rs 88.16 cr; the equity raise is a funding question to research.

label: KIRIINDUS
rationale: Commercial production started on 25 Jan 2021, which is firm and not yet in reported results; a specialty intermediates plant may open a new revenue stream, though the packet does not establish that. The packet gives no capacity or revenue figure, so size is unknown and cannot be shown to reach 10% of TTM revenue of Rs 892.37 crore. Watch for the first revenue and capacity disclosure; the trigger text was not extracted, so the scope rests on one sentence.

label: GUFICBIO
rationale: The Q3 profit surge is partly from two prefilled-syringe brands already launched, so that part is in reported results and is not new. The forward items are management plans (5 products in FY2021-22, a September 2021 filing and an FY2023-24 launch for a recombinant candidate) that are not firm and not sized against TTM revenue of INR 400.49 cr. The company is profitable with no heavy losses, so the plan is credible and company-specific enough to watch, and the milestone is the first product launch or filing; no disqualifier applies.

label: ENDURANCE
rationale: The Vallam plant augments die-casting capacity and brings brake components in-house, both within lines the company already runs. The packet gives no capex, capacity or revenue, so size against TTM revenue of INR 6,011 crore is unknown. This is routine capacity extension, not a new product, customer or revenue stream, so reject.

label: CENTURYPLY
rationale: The Rs 200 crore Hoshiarpur MDF expansion is a company-specific capacity plan, so it is not firm, and it would be a new MDF capacity addition rather than routine flow. Size against revenue is unknown because Rs 200 crore is capex and the packet gives no incremental capacity or realisation. The Q3 operating-profit jump is mostly recovery from a weak prior-year quarter with no identified operating mechanism, so it does not itself qualify. Watch for board approval and a stated capacity and revenue ramp.

label: UNICHEMLAB
rationale: The Apremilast ANDA approval is firm regulatory approval, but no value or quantity is stated, so size against TTM revenue of INR 1,281.29 cr is unknown. It is the third ANDA approval in about five weeks after Celecoxib and Zonisamide, which makes it routine flow for this generics business rather than a step-change. The 1,501 bps margin rise has no identified commercial mechanism, so the case is rejected.

label: SSWL
rationale: Firm INR 14.6 crore export order equals about 1.0% of trailing-four-quarter revenue of INR 1,437 crore, and the EUR order is smaller still. The company announces similar export orders regularly (22,000 and 26,000 wheel orders in January 2021 plus a long list of earlier orders in status updates), so this is routine flow and immaterial. No disqualifier applies; trailing PAT is only marginally negative and the last two quarters were profitable.

label: PIIND
rationale: The company is only geared up to commence commercial production for a new customer, so production has not started and the event is not firm under 3.3. A new customer for the company is not routine, and the company is well funded after a QIP. Size is unknown against TTM revenue of INR 4,235 crore because no value or quantity is stated, so the milestone is the start of commercial production for this customer.

label: APOLLOTYRE
rationale: Size is unknown in value terms, but a 2-3% price increase on replacement and OE sales implies a ceiling well under 10% of TTM revenue of about Rs 15,920 cr. The price increases are in effect, but pass-through pricing is ordinary flow for a tyre maker and the 707 bps margin gain is already in reported Q3FY21 results. Debt reduction from shareholder money is not an operating driver, and the product launch has no demand evidence in the packet.

label: SUBEXLTD
rationale: Size is unknown: the packet states no contract value or volume, and the trailing revenue needed for a comparison is missing. The wins are firm as contracts won, but management describes them as steady progress in new project initiation, which reads as the ordinary flow of business rather than a step-change. Routine, so reject; the packet is too thin for a stronger call.

label: NITCO
rationale: Operating margin rose 1,085 bps to -2.1% but remains negative, and the launches are a non-exclusive tie-up and a 4-counter retail launch with no value disclosed. The company is loss-making (TTM PAT INR -90.74 cr on INR 287.5 cr revenue) with about INR 54 cr of annualised finance cost, so the heavy-losses-plus-high-debt STRESSED disqualifier applies and the launches are not the fix. The event is also immaterial.

label: INE312H01016
rationale: The trigger is the opening of one leased multiplex in Kolkata, with no stated revenue and no financial snapshot to size against, so size is unknown. Opening screens and multiplexes is this chain's normal flow (the packet's own capex note is about completing screens), so the event is routine rather than a step-change. The capacity ambition is non-binding and no disqualifier applies, but nothing in the packet makes this material.

label: TITAGARH
rationale: The firm Rs 174.76 crore Indian Navy contract, a total value over a period to Aug 2023, is about 11.6% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,503 crore (9.9% of FY2020 revenue), so it clears the 10% test on the trailing basis. It is a new customer and a new vessel product line, so it is not routine even though the company regularly wins wagon orders. No disqualifier applies: the trailing loss and consolidated net debt are margin and funding questions for deep research rather than a stress that prevents capture of the award.

label: NILAINFRA
rationale: The two AMC awards total INR 88.33 crore of estimated development cost over 24 months, about 62.4% of TTM revenue of INR 141.60 crore; the multi-year total is compared per rule 3.3. The release says AMC awarded them, so they count as firm, though the packet tags the amount non-binding and the award letter has not been seen. They are not routine given no comparable award and a sharp revenue decline; losses are small and debt is not in the packet, so this is not a stressed case.

label: DHANUKA
rationale: The Dahej technical-pesticide plant is a board-approved plan, so it is not firm; it is credible and company-specific, but its capacity and revenue are not stated, so size against TTM revenue (1,339.48 cr) is unknown. The Q3 margin gain, which the packet could not explain, is attributed by management to operating leverage on 9 percent revenue growth, which is business as usual. The new products are management statements; watch for commissioning with capacity disclosed.

label: MSTCLTD
rationale: Every order event is unquantified, so size against TTM revenue of 663.13 crore cannot be established. The cotton mandate is described by the company as hard to win, and the other events are MoUs or portal certification rather than firm orders. The large margin and finance-cost moves are financial changes with no operating explanation in the packet, which the rules treat as a reject. Routine status of auction-agency mandates is unknown from the packet.

label: NOCIL
rationale: The INR 280 crore capex is 34 percent of TTM revenue of INR 815.33 crore, but it was commissioned in June 2018 and January 2019, so its effect is already in the reported revenue and profit (fatal flaw: already fully in reported results). The packet shows no new capacity, customer or market, and the company's revenue is a business-as-usual base. No deep research is warranted.

label: VIYASH
rationale: The customer-qualification trigger is a CEP approval for one generic API, which the release calls the company's 11th such EDQM approval, so it is regular flow rather than a change. No value or revenue is stated, so size against TTM revenue (1,315.33 cr) is unknown. The finance-cost fall comes from term-loan prepayment and the margin gain has no stated link to the approval, so REJECT as routine.

label: SHIVATEX
rationale: The Rs 13.62 crore Ministry of Defence rucksack order is firm but about 4% of TTM revenue of Rs 321 crore, well below the 10% test. It is a small supply order that cannot explain the Q3 margin or profit improvement, which has no operating explanation in the packet. The company's recent product launches are pandemic-era, so there is no durable inflection to research.

label: FORTIS
rationale: Size is estimated at about 1.6% of trailing revenue (250 beds x 50% occupancy x an assumed Rs0.5 crore revenue per occupied bed-year, about Rs62.5 crore against TTM revenue of Rs3,890.60 crore), well below the 10% threshold. The facility is firm (commissioned October 2020), but adding hospital beds is the company's normal capacity flow and its contribution is already in the December 2020 quarter. Rejected as business as usual and below materiality.

label: HEROMOTOCO
rationale: The Harley-Davidson alliance (a new premium brand line) and the Mexico entry (a new market) are non-routine and company-specific, but neither has a stated volume, value or launch date, so neither is firm. The reported profit rise is volume and cost driven in the existing business and does not qualify on its own. Size against trailing consolidated revenue of Rs 28,603 cr cannot be estimated. The milestone is the first commercial launch or first Mexico sales with disclosed volumes.

label: INE244J01017
rationale: The deck shows the same three per-annum orders, INR 86 crore in total, as the other Rane group filings, but this packet has no revenue, price or symbol, so size cannot be computed and it is not established that this entity executes them. The company cannot be confirmed as a listed, reporting business from this packet, so it needs data repair before any triage judgment.

label: NCC
rationale: The Rs 1,200 crore January order is firm and about 16% of trailing revenue of INR 7,467 crore, but NCC wins orders of this size regularly (five orders in one month, and a cumulative INR 50,000 crore book over several years), so it is routine flow rather than a step-change. The margin gain and finance-cost fall are attributed to lower debt utilisation and bank terms, not an operating event, and the equity warrants are financing. No deep research.

label: CAMLINFINE
rationale: The product launch is observed, but the slide shows the North America subsidiary's operating revenue at only a few hundred INR million at most, which is small against TTM group revenue of INR 1,153.35 cr. The margin and profit rise has no identified operating event, so it fails the mechanism test and is a financial change without an operating explanation. No disqualifier applies, but the event is immaterial on the packet evidence.

label: INE455T01018
rationale: Size cannot be computed: the packet has no revenue, so the derived ~150 crore reduction has no base. The trigger amount is wrong (1,869 crore is the balance). Tradeability cannot be checked (no symbol, no prices). Repair the event amount and pull results and listing status before any triage decision.

label: SUZLON
rationale: The event is a debt restructuring that lowered finance cost, but its value is not stated and part of the fall is non-cash. The company is loss-making (TTM PAT -676.38 cr on TTM revenue 2,864.82 cr) with heavy debt, so the restructuring is a balance-sheet change that does not address the operating losses and is not an earnings inflection. The STRESSED disqualifier applies.

label: LT
rationale: Neither event has a stated value, and the Mauritius extension is 3.4 km of metro line; no item in the packet approaches 10% of trailing revenue of Rs 132,136 cr (threshold Rs 13,214 cr). The packet lists a steady run of large disclosed orders in January 2021 (for example the HRRL EPCC contracts, the High Speed Rail order and Rail Vikas Nigam), so these are routine flow for a company of this scale. No inflection is shown.

label: UTIAMC
rationale: The trigger is a bank distribution empanelment that is standing business for an asset manager, with no value, AUM or quantity stated, so size is unknown. It is routine channel activity, not a change, and the same call says the company lost fixed-income market share. The packet has no trailing revenue to size against, so there is no deep research case.

label: BIRLANU
rationale: Event value is INR 23 crore of debt repaid in the quarter, about 0.8% of trailing revenue of INR 2,845 crore; the launch and Faridabad plant are unquantified. The year-on-year jump is largely a low-base and pent-up-demand effect, and management itself warns that next year faces a tough comparison. The debt repayment is a financing effect, so this is a financial change without a clear operating event under the rule. Revisit if the Humid Cure or Faridabad plant produces quantified revenue.

label: INE872A01014
rationale: The Rs 7.92 crore item is a reversal of interest accrued in an earlier quarter, already booked in reported Sep-2020 results, so it is a period item and noise rather than a future earnings change. The packet has no revenue or price figures, so size against revenue is unknown. The item is not an operating event and is rejected as a fatal flaw.

label: IRCON
rationale: The largest order, INR 900 crore, is firm and about 18.8% of TTM revenue of INR 4,794 crore, and the Q3 total of INR 1,623 crore is about 34%. Five similar railway and highway EPC awards in one quarter, plus a rising revenue base, show regular order flow for an infra EPC company rather than a change in trajectory. Profits are already positive, so there is no stress or inflection, and the route is reject.

label: ASTRAL
rationale: Size is unknown: the tank business revenue is not disclosed, and the Rs 51 crore acquisition consideration is a balance-sheet amount, not revenue, so it cannot size the event. The line is firm because billing started on 12 Dec 2020, and water-storage tanks are a new product line for the company, so it is not routine. The packet's solar trigger is immaterial, so the tank revenue run-rate and the Orissa plant start are the milestones to watch.

label: PRAKASH
rationale: The gross-margin gain has no identified operating event and the debt reduction is a promoter equity infusion, so neither is a change in operating earnings trajectory. The packet has no stated event value or quantity, so size against trailing revenue of INR 2,831 crore is unknown. The catalyst is also stale (waiting 173 days) with no new operating evidence.

label: DRREDDY
rationale: Size is unknown: the packet states no value for the facility's US qualification, and it is not a quantity of a product, so no estimate is possible against TTM revenue of INR 18,728 crore. The FDA EIR was issued in April/May 2020 and the pricing and acquisition gains are already in the Q1-Q3 FY21 reported revenue (fatal flaw: already in reported results). Quarterly revenue growth of 2.0% to 14.7% YoY are business-as-usual recovery rather than a new revenue stream, so there is no deep-research case.

label: PDSL
rationale: The debt reduction is Rs 144 crore, about 2.3% of trailing revenue of 6,262.82 crore, and is a balance-sheet change with no operating explanation. The product-launch bullet is a single unquantified line in an investor presentation with no revenue, demand or margin evidence, so it is not a credible change in trajectory. Neither event qualifies for research or watch.

label: SUTLEJTEX
rationale: The Baddi unit is credible and company-specific but not firm: it is in trial production with COD only guided for March 2021. Its 120 MT/day capacity (about 43,800 t a year at full output) is about 65 percent captive, which replaces purchases rather than adding revenue, and no external sales volume or price is stated, so size against TTM revenue (1,743.31 cr) is unknown. The Ikea approval is supplier qualification, not an order, and the company is loss-making, so watch for COD and disclosed external sales.

label: SUNTECK
rationale: The Rs 53 crore repayment is about 10.6% of TTM revenue of 499.67 crore, but it is a debt repayment from cash flow on a base the company itself calls negligible. It is a balance-sheet change, not a change in future earnings or the operating trajectory. Rejected as a financial change with no operating explanation.

label: PPAP
rationale: Supplies for new models at existing OEM customers are the normal flow for an auto-component supplier, and the packet states no value or quantity, so size against TTM revenue of INR 312 crore is unknown. The profit rise tracks revenue growth of 36.5% and shows no single step-change. This is routine business as usual, so reject.

label: KOLTEPATIL
rationale: The Rs83 crore net debt reduction is about 13.4% of trailing revenue of Rs617.40 crore, so size clears 10%, but it is a balance-sheet repayment rather than an operating change. The operating profit and margin jump has no identified commercial mechanism in the packet, and the trailing PAT is negative. Rejected as a financial change with no operating explanation, a judgment call given the size.

label: GMRAIRPORT
rationale: The airport items are letters of intent, which are not firm, and carry no stated value. The company is stressed: trailing PAT is Rs -3,831 cr, trailing finance cost is about Rs 3,456 cr against Rs 6,163 cr revenue, and debt reduction is still unquantified. The LoIs do not fix this, so the stressed-company disqualifier applies.

label: GLOBUSSPR
rationale: No firm order is shown: the trigger events are a product launch with no revenue commitment and a debt reduction from paring finance costs, which is not operating. The 1,506 bps margin rise and 52.5% revenue growth have no disclosed mechanism, and a court-convened scheme in the same window may explain them through consolidation, which the packet cannot separate. Under the rule, a financial change with no operating explanation is rejected.

label: KNRCON
rationale: The Rs 5,389 million EPC order is firm and about 20% of TTM revenue, but KNR wins large state road orders regularly: Rs 604 crore on 4 Jan 2021 and Rs 1,157 crore in the prior quarter. For a road EPC company whose order flow is a multiple of revenue, an order of this size is routine. No disqualifier applies, but routine flow rules it out.

label: NBCC
rationale: Firm INR 1,800 crore order from the Rajasthan government, about 27% of trailing consolidated revenue of INR 6,765 crore; treated as the group's own external order under the pass-through rule. It is routine for this company: management calls its recent awards very high value, cites an INR 8,000 crore Amrapali award and INR 500-600 crore projects, so this order sits within its normal flow. The healthcare push is a stated plan with no disclosed pipeline, so nothing shows a step-change; reject unless healthcare orders show a new revenue line.

label: COALINDIA
rationale: The stated amount of Rs 13,277 cr is 14.6% of trailing revenue of Rs 90,894.10 cr, but the work orders are shown as awarded to Talcher Fertilizers Limited, not to Coal India, so they are not Coal India's firm order (fatal flaw: belongs to someone else). The award dates from Sept 2019 and appears on a results-call slide, so it is also old, not a new event. Reject.

label: BATAINDIA
rationale: Size is unknown: the packet gives neither an order value nor a quantity. The orders are ordinary institutional-channel sales recovering as COVID restrictions eased, which is routine flow and a recovery effect rather than a change in trajectory. The product launch is a marketing campaign with no revenue commitment. Trailing PAT is Rs -80.38 cr, which the event does not explain, so no inflection is shown.

label: VBL
rationale: Mountain Dew Ice is a flavour variant of an existing franchise line, which is routine product flow, and the packet gives no revenue, volume or price for it. The finance-cost decline is a financial change attributed to debt repayment with no operating event, and the gross-margin gain has no stated cause. Revenue grew 9% in the quarter, so there is no material change to research.

label: SHAILY
rationale: Firm: commercial production has started at the steel furniture plant. Non-routine: a new plant adding an output line, with no earlier comparable disclosure in the packet. Size is unknown because the packet has no financials, so no revenue denominator exists to test the 10 percent bar, and no capacity is stated to estimate from. Watch until capacity and first revenue are disclosed.

label: ASTRON
rationale: The profit rise comes from ordinary price pass-through in a commodity paper cycle, not a discrete company-specific event, and no price or volume amount is stated. Trailing revenue is Rs 391 cr and trailing PAT Rs 6.3 cr. Reject as routine cyclical pricing with no quantified or non-routine change.

label: CEMPRO
rationale: Two awards secured after 31 Dec 2020 total Rs 530.6 cr (Rs 376.9 cr Calcutta High Court bench, Rs 153.7 cr Pamban Bridge substructure), about 21% of trailing revenue Rs 2,483 cr, and they are firm. The company wins orders this size routinely: its Rs 12,032 cr order book is 4.8 times TTM revenue and a single Rs 1,142.5 cr award was secured in the December quarter, so this is business as usual, not an inflection. The unexplained 650 bps gross-margin gain is a financial change with no operating explanation in the packet, and the stressed test cannot be closed without debt data.

label: UNOMINDA
rationale: Size is unknown: no order value is stated and the packet gives no order-inflow history to size against TTM revenue of Rs 5,023 cr. New orders from existing OEM customers are normal flow for an auto-component supplier, so they are not a change from business as usual. The Q3 profit jump is a results-level move with no specific operating event attributed, and the debt repayment is financing rather than operating. Reject as routine flow with no sized event.

label: GUJENERGY
rationale: The stated 988 cr prepayment is 10.65% of TTM revenue (9,275.14 cr), but it is a balance-sheet repayment whose earnings effect is only a lower finance cost (about 22 cr a quarter year on year), not a change in operations. The Q3 margin and operating-profit gains have no operating mechanism in the packet. This is a financial change with no operating explanation, so REJECT.

label: NUCLEUS
rationale: No event is identified: the trigger is a year-on-year operating margin increase (up 834 bps to 24.6%) and the packet's own why-now records no mechanism. Against FY2020 revenue of Rs 520.83 cr there is no event value to size, so size is unknown and nothing is firm. Under the decision rule a financial change with no operating explanation is REJECT_WITH_REASON; no listed disqualifier applies.

label: HGS
rationale: The Rs 51 crore gross debt repayment is about 1% of trailing revenue of Rs 5,311.03 crore, so it is immaterial. Repaying debt is ordinary balance-sheet management, and the packet shows no operating event behind it, so this is a financial change with no operating explanation. Reject.

label: GABRIEL
rationale: The ISUZU export order is firm but shows no value, and export OEM supply is the company's normal business, so it is routine. The 200-plus SKU launch follows 150 SKUs launched last year and more than 850 in five years, so it is also routine. Size against TTM revenue of INR 1,544 crore cannot be established and nothing shows a step-change, so the packet is rejected.

label: MEP
rationale: The awards are firm letters of award and tolling has started, but the contract value and size against TTM revenue of 1,261.90 crore are unknown. Toll collection is the company's normal business, so the awards are routine flow. The company is stressed, with TTM PAT of -39.08 crore and finance cost of about 88 crore a quarter, so it is unlikely to capture the benefit. The margin rise the packet links to these orders predates them.

label: PAGEIND
rationale: The debt repayment is a balance-sheet change with no revenue effect. The pricing item is an undecided price increase, so it is not firm, and management says it takes one price increase every year, which is routine. The 691 bps margin rise has no identified mechanism and no quantified size against TTM revenue of INR 2,493 cr, so the case is rejected.

label: BLUESTARCO
rationale: The Wada plant is a non-binding plan, not commissioned, and its Rs 130 cr is capex spend, which does not size revenue; no capacity quantity is given, so size is unknown. The plant and the range launches extend existing commercial refrigeration and water-cooler lines, which is the company's normal flow rather than a new revenue stream, and against TTM revenue of Rs 3,951 cr the packet shows no operating event that could explain the Q3 profit rise with revenue down 9.1%. This is a financial change with no operating explanation, so REJECT_WITH_REASON.

label: CONFIPET
rationale: Size estimated at about 0.13%: one MRU at an assumed INR 1 crore a year gives 1 crore against TTM revenue of 789.74 crore. The contract is firm, but immaterial at this scale. The company is profitable with low finance cost, and there is no disqualifier; the rejection rests on size alone.

label: AHLADA
rationale: Size vs revenue is unknown because no financials are public by the cutoff. The Rs 38.31 cr award is 1.7x the Rs 22.47 cr Government of Andhra Pradesh order of 7 Jan 2021, and the same counterparty pattern recurs, so it is one of several similar orders and routine. Reject as routine flow.

label: TALBROAUTO
rationale: The press release states about INR 92 crore over the contract life; Talbros's 50% share (about INR 46 crore) is 12.2% of TTM revenue of INR 378.20 crore, using the multi-year total with the period unstated. The annual figure (about 1.9% at share) is much smaller, so the case depends on the contract life. Supplies have started, so it is firm, and no comparable order is disclosed in the packet, so it is not routine on this evidence; no disqualifier applies, but the period and JV share must be confirmed.

label: DALBHARAT
rationale: The 3 MnTPA clinker plant is firm, having started commercial production in October 2020. Its estimated value of about INR 225 crore (1.5 MnT at 50 percent utilisation, times INR 1,500 per tonne) is 2.3 percent of TTM revenue, far below the 10 percent threshold, and it is partly captive. The debt repayment is financing, and the profit gain is largely unexplained by the plant, so this is immaterial.

label: NATCOPHARM
rationale: The trigger is a facility-profile slide restating a US FDA EIR received in 2019 (investor presentation pages 11 and 13, read with the page command), so it is track-record noise rather than a new 2021 event. No value or product quantity is disclosed, so size is unknown. With no new approval and revenue swings that the EIR does not explain, this is rejected as a fatal flaw (noise and track record).

label: DEEPAKFERT
legal_name: Deepak Fertilizers and Petrochemicals Corporation Limited
rationale: Commercial production of a new HANFO cartridge line has started, so it is firm, and a forward-integration product line is non-routine. Pages 2-5 of the Q3 results press release (read with the page command) give no value, volume or capacity for it, so size against TTM revenue of INR 5,526.36 cr is unknown, and the line may well be immaterial. The margin and finance-cost moves are tied to collections and realisations rather than this line, so the case is watch-only until revenue or volume is disclosed.

label: ASHOKA
rationale: Size is 10.4% of trailing revenue (INR 503 crore against TTM revenue of INR 4,840 crore), a stated value. The order is firm (binding demand), but a single EPC order of this size is the normal flow for an EPC contractor, so it is routine; the packet gives no order-inflow history to show otherwise, and that judgement is the swing factor. The company is heavily indebted but profitable on a TTM basis, so no stress disqualifier applies.

label: SIS
rationale: Net debt reduction of Rs213 crore is about 2.4% of trailing-four-quarter revenue of Rs8,892 crore (size stated, firm as a completed reduction). The change is a balance-sheet deleveraging with no operating explanation, and the lower finance cost is already in reported results, so it is a financial change rather than an earnings inflection. Rejected on size and absence of an operating trigger.

label: ZYDUSWELL
rationale: Size: the Rs 1,500 cr redemption is 85.8% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,749 cr as a balance-sheet amount, but the earnings effect is the finance-cost saving of about Rs 21 cr in the quarter, which is a financial change. The source of the redemption funds is not stated, and the packet shows no operating explanation for the profit move. Reject as a financial change with no operating explanation; the debt route is not an operating inflection.

label: CAPLIPOINT
rationale: The USFDA approval is firm but is one of a routine stream of approvals (seven US launches so far and four more ANDA approvals expected), and its value is not stated. The LatAm tenders are non-binding and described as emergency procurement, so they are not firm and may be one-off. The margin jump coincides with a 46% fall in quarterly revenue and has no disclosed operating driver, so no change in trajectory is shown against trailing revenue of Rs 608.91 cr.

label: JBMA
rationale: The Letter of Award from Delhi Transport Corporation is a firm external order for 700 buses. Estimated at INR 280 cr (700 buses x assumed INR 40 lakh per bus), it is about 16.4% of trailing revenue of INR 1,712.37 cr. The packet shows no comparable earlier orders, so it is not routine, and no disqualifier applies, though the 53.7% revenue jump needs an acquisition or reclassification check.

label: PPL
rationale: CPVC production has commenced at Kashipur, which is firm (commercial production started) and a new product line, so it is not routine. No CPVC value, volume, capacity or price is disclosed, so size against FY20 revenue of INR 389.2 cr cannot be estimated, and the quarter's growth is not attributed to CPVC. The 65,000 MTPA expansion is a plan, not firm; with firm, non-routine and unsized, this is WATCH_MILESTONE, and the milestone is the first disclosed CPVC sales.

label: SETCO
rationale: No value or quantity is stated for the new farm-tractor clutch supplies, so size against TTM revenue of INR 342 crore is unknown. The commercial start is firm and the farm-tractor line is new, but the company is stressed: TTM PAT is -INR 75 crore, finance cost runs at about INR 13-16 crore per quarter against quarterly revenue of INR 41-111 crore, and the packet records a debt restructuring. The restructuring is not the event itself, so the STRESSED disqualifier applies.

label: SOBHA
rationale: Size is unknown: the launch states no value, capex or quantity, so no percentage of FY20 revenue (INR 3,753.90 cr) or TTM revenue (INR 2,466.50 cr) can be computed. It is not firm because there is no evidence of sales, orders or commercial operation, though a new consumer furniture line would be non-routine if it reached sales. The packet shows a company-specific milestone that could be watched, with first disclosed furniture revenue or orders as the milestone; no disqualifier is established, as TTM PAT is positive, though the finance cost is heavy against PBT.

label: ELGIEQUIP
rationale: The only trigger is a net debt level of INR 109 crore, a balance-sheet statement rather than a change in future earnings, and no reduction amount or operating event is stated. The 90% operating profit rise and margin gain have no identified mechanism, which the rules treat as a financial change with no operating explanation. The trailing base also includes the COVID-hit June 2020 quarter, so the recovery may be a low-base effect. No deep research.

label: CRISIL
rationale: The only trigger is the ICON platform launch, with no disclosed value, client count or demand, so it is not shown to be firm. Even if ICON were the whole Advisory segment (Rs 134.1 cr of 2020 income, 6.8% of trailing revenue of Rs 1,981.83 cr), it could not reach the 10% threshold, so it is immaterial on the packet's own numbers. The operating-profit rise has no identified mechanism and is not evidence of an inflection.

label: ACC
rationale: Estimated at 50% utilisation and Rs 3,500 per tonne, the commissioned Sindri unit (1.4 MTPA, about Rs 245 crore a year, 1.8% of TTM revenue of Rs 13,786 crore) and the Ametha plan (2.7 MTPA, about 3.4%) together come to about 5%, far below 10% and routine capacity addition for a cement company. The only order is a related-party supply agreement with Ambuja Cements, which is internal demand. The margin and finance-cost gains are a financial change with no operating explanation.

label: JAYSREETEA
rationale: The Rs 50 crore debt reduction is about 6.4% of TTM revenue of 782.24 crore (19.2% if the 150 crore reading is correct), but it is a financial deleveraging via asset sales with no operating driver. The company is loss making (TTM PAT -25.94 crore) and carries debt, so it is stressed and unlikely to capture any benefit, which is a disqualifier. Rejected.

label: AARVI
rationale: The 53 crore order is stated and is about 24.8% of TTM revenue of INR 213.46 crore; no execution period is given, so the stated total is used. It is firm as a won order and not routine on the packet's disclosures, since it is the largest order disclosed and 1.7x the next-largest in the quarter. The same quarter also shows 30.69 crore and 8.2 crore wins and 10+ new contracts, so routine flow is a real risk, which is why confidence is low.

label: KANSAINER
rationale: Size is unknown: no revenue or volume is disclosed for the three launched products, against TTM revenue of INR 4,695 cr. The launches are in commercial operation, but three decorative product refreshes are normal flow for a paint company, and the packet's Q3 profit rise sits alongside 19.6% YoY revenue growth, which points to demand recovery rather than a change in trajectory. No disqualifier is assigned, and the company is funded (TTM PAT INR 467 cr), so the event is rejected as routine.

label: ADVENZYMES
rationale: The only operating catalyst is a non-binding management ceiling that the expanded SSPL business could reach about Rs 100 crore of revenue, roughly 21% of trailing group revenue of Rs 478.9 crore if achieved, which would clear the size test. It is not firm, so it is watch-only until the expansion is approved or commissioned and audited revenue is disclosed. The Rs 16 crore debt repayment and margin and finance-cost gains are financial changes and do not qualify on their own.

label: INE674A01014
rationale: A stated net debt reduction of Rs 495 crore exists in the investor presentation, but the packet has no revenue, so size cannot be expressed against revenue. Tradeability is unverified (no symbol, no prices), the source of the reduction is truncated, and the counterparty field is corrupted. Repair the packet before triage.

label: REPCOHOME
rationale: The event is a debt redemption of Rs 272 crore, about 19.6% of trailing four-quarter revenue of 1,385.91 crore, so it is sized and completed. It is a balance-sheet financial change, not an operating event; any interest saving is a financial effect with no operating explanation in the packet. Per the rules, a financial change with no operating explanation is rejected, and the finance cost check could not be verified.

label: SALZERELEC
rationale: The secured Australia/New Zealand contract is firm on management's statement and is non-routine because the company had not served that market, but it has no stated value. The only stated value, USD 4-5 million of additional export business with no period, is about 5.8 percent of TTM revenue (Rs 568 crore) at an assumed Rs 73.5 per USD, which is below the 10 percent threshold. The wire harness ramp is operating but largely already in reported results, and the price pass-through is not an inflection. Watch for the contract value and first revenue in Q1 FY22.

label: INE676A01019
rationale: Stated contract values sum to more than US$64 mn over 2 to 6 year periods, but the packet has no revenue or financial snapshot, so the percentage of revenue is not computed. The wins are several similar managed-services and data-centre deals in one quarter's highlights, which is routine flow for an IT services business. No disqualifier is shown, but the packet's name and symbol data do not establish that the security still trades and should be repaired before any later research.

label: INDIANHUME
rationale: The stated Rs 162.23 cr is 13.75% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,179.66 cr, but it is only an L1 position, so it is not firm. The order book of Rs 4,691.57 cr is about four times TTM revenue and grew by about Rs 1,030 cr in the year, so annual order inflow is a multiple of revenue and a project of this size is the company's normal flow, which makes it routine. REJECT_WITH_REASON.

label: SADBHIN
rationale: Provisional COD on unnamed road projects is a firm operating start, but no value or quantity is given, so size against revenue is unknown. The company is stressed: losses in every quarter except the Mar-2020 quarter (which was flattered by an exceptional gain), finance costs of INR 211-345 crore a quarter, a debt restructuring, and new debentures to repay debt. The fix needed is financing, not the projects, so the STRESSED disqualifier applies.

label: AURIONPRO
rationale: The release describes a bank selection and the exchange filing calls it an order, which we treat as firm, but it states no value, term or rollout scope, so size against revenue is unknown (TTM revenue about Rs 369 crore). Whether it is more than the company's usual flow is not established from the packet, and the Q3 margin expansion predates this announcement and is not explained by it. Watch for a disclosed contract value or rollout scope before any deep research; no disqualifier applies, and the thin trading liquidity is not one.

label: CHAMBLFERT
rationale: The trigger is a government subsidy allocation that reduces debt and finance cost, which is a financial change rather than an operating one. The quarterly finance cost saving of about Rs 57 cr is an annualised effect of roughly 1.7% of trailing revenue of Rs 13,047 cr, below the 10% threshold, and the amount of the allocation is not stated in the packet. The margin gain has no identified operating mechanism, so no inflection is shown.

label: RPPINFRA
rationale: The 174.03 crore order is a firm award to RPP's 49% JV; RPP's share (about INR 85 crore) is 17.3% of TTM revenue of INR 492.44 crore, above the 10% line. It is the first firm order disclosed in the packet, so it is not routine on this evidence, though the later 157.87 and 176.58 crore orders are similar in size and their routine status is untested. The company is profitable, so the rights issue is a funding question rather than a stress disqualifier.

label: ESTER
rationale: The new product line has started commercial sales, which counts as firm, and a new product line is not routine. Its size is unknown: the packet gives no product revenue, no volume and no trailing annual revenue, so it cannot be placed against the 10 percent threshold, and the most this allows is watch. The 26.8 crore debt repayment is a balance-sheet event and is rejected under 3.3 as a financial change, and the INR 587 crore capex is non-binding and not firm.

label: BLIL
rationale: The only trigger passage is OCR-garbled text that the page-6 read shows to be a labour-code and gratuity disclosure, not an order, so the event is noise and a fatal flaw. There is no order value or quantity, and the packet has no financials to size against. Nothing in the packet shows a change from business as usual.

label: PNCINFRA
rationale: The INR 881 crore COD is 16.7 percent of TTM revenue of INR 5,270 crore, and the six EPC awards are firm. A road EPC contractor that completes projects and wins several EPC contracts at a time is business as usual, so the event is routine rather than a change in trajectory. The margin and profit gains are a COVID-recovery base effect with a weak operating link to the awards, so there is no deep-research case.

label: EVEREADY
rationale: Size is unknown: the only commercial item is an unquantified battery and flashlight price increase to offset rupee depreciation, and no value or quantity is given. It is not firm and not a change from business as usual: page 14 attributes the margin gain (11.3% to 20.1%) to mix, lower distribution, promotional and overhead spend during COVID restrictions, and currency pass-through pricing. These effects are temporary or cyclical and already in reported Q3 results, so the financial change has an operating explanation that does not indicate a trajectory change. Rejected.

label: APARINDS
rationale: The 450 crore order is firm and stated and equals about 7.1% of TTM revenue of 6,302.33 crore, below the 10% threshold. The packet has no earlier order history, so routine status cannot be tested, and nothing in it shows a path from this order to material revenue. The capacity item is a management expectation, and the margin and operating-profit rise in the Dec 2020 quarter has no identified mechanism and predates the order.

label: BAJAJCON
rationale: The only trigger is a finance-cost decline of about INR 0.9 crore, a financial change with no operating explanation, and the packet names no order, capacity or product event. The proposed rights issue is equity financing, not an operating change. Trailing revenue is INR 852 crore and no event value exists to size against it, so there is no inflection to research.

label: RUPA
rationale: A premium-brand launch is a credible, company-specific candidate for a 370 bps margin gain, but the pages read give no premium-brand sales or margin and the launches read as ongoing strategy, so nothing is firm. Quarterly revenue grew only 5-12%, so the margin gain is not tied to a material revenue line and size is unknown. Watch for disclosure of premium-brand sales.

label: APEX
rationale: The trigger describes moving existing processing from a leased facility to a new plant, with no added capacity, product or customer stated, so it is not a revenue step-change. No value or quantity is given, so size against TTM revenue of INR 777 crore is unknown. The December-quarter profit fall runs against any upside, so reject as routine operations.

label: ZENTEC
rationale: The trigger is a finance cost drop (Rs 0.17 cr in the latest quarter) and a gross margin rise, both with no operating event; the packet attributes the debt reduction to equity raised in the lookback, which is financing, not earnings. Revenue is falling sharply, so there is no operating inflection in the packet. No event value exists, size is unknown, and nothing is firm, so this is REJECT_WITH_REASON for a financial change with no operating explanation.

label: TIMETECHNO
rationale: The recorded value of Rs 809 crore is the total debt level, about 27.2% of TTM revenue of 2,969.87 crore, but the passage shows the actual reduction was about Rs 23 crore (roughly 0.8% of TTM revenue). A small debt reduction with no operating explanation is a financial change, so it is rejected.

label: AMBUJACEM
rationale: The grinding unit is commissioned, so it is firm, but at 1.4 MTPA the estimated value (INR 280 cr at 50% utilisation and an assumed INR 4,000 per tonne) is about 1.1% of trailing revenue of INR 24,516 cr, which is immaterial with no plausible path to 10%. The ACC master supply agreement is an intra-group renewal on unchanged terms, which is internal demand and not an inflection. The margin and finance-cost moves are explained in part by the special-products mix and cost savings, so the case is rejected.

label: DYNAMATECH
rationale: The change is a board-approved refinancing that lowers interest cost, which is a financial change with no operating explanation. Its size is not stated, and the finance cost fall is modest relative to trailing revenue of Rs 1,138 cr. Reject as an immaterial financial change; the separate JKM Ferrotech asset sale is not sized in the packet.

label: NACLIND
rationale: Commercial production of two new granular formulations is firm and a new product line is not routine, but the packet gives no value and no demand evidence, so size against TTM revenue of INR 1,138 crore is unknown. The promoter loan repayment is financing under 3.3 and is not an operating event. The margin gain has no operating explanation in the packet beyond the launches, so the milestone is revenue disclosure from the new formulations.

label: PENINLAND
rationale: Size is stated: Rs 430 crore against TTM revenue of 481.15 crore (89.4%), and the reduction is firm (pledge invoked July 2020). It is disqualified as stressed: the company is loss-making (TTM PAT -260.29 crore), its NCDs were enforced by a debenture trustee, and the debt cut came from losing a subsidiary investment rather than from earnings. The event does not restore the earnings base.

label: INE222J01013
rationale: The deck states three secured orders worth INR 86 crore a year in total, but with no revenue base the size against revenue cannot be computed. The identical three lines appear in four Rane group filings, so it is not clear which entity holds them, and no exchange symbol or price is on record. The company cannot be established as a listed, reporting business from this packet, so the case needs data repair before any triage judgment.

label: MONTECARLO
rationale: The trigger value of Rs 1,472 million (147.2 crore, 23.6% of standalone TTM revenue of 622.72 crore) is a cash balance in the investor presentation, not a debt repayment; the same slide shows long-term borrowing of only Rs 128.7 million. The event is a misread and a fatal flaw. No change to earnings is evidenced, and the margin and finance cost moves have no stated operating explanation.

label: TATAPOWER
rationale: The NESCO item is a conditional letter of intent, so it is not firm; the milestone is the final OERC licence. Size is estimated from the 5,450 MU input energy at an assumed INR 4.0/kWh, about INR 2,180 cr or 7.5% of TTM revenue (28,961.51 cr), which is below 10% even if firm, so the outcome is watch. It would be a new distribution revenue line, so it is not routine. The 4,150 cr bank-loan repayment is a financial change with no operating event and is rejected; the solar awards are firm but routine.

label: MARKSANS
rationale: Gross margin rose 925 bps and operating profit 92.6% YoY on TTM revenue of INR 1,381.33 cr and TTM PAT of INR 201.78 cr, so the financial change is real. The only stated operating cause is an unnamed launch and a generic UK/USA pipeline with no product, size or timing, so nothing is firm and size cannot be stated. Debt repayment is a financial change and does not qualify on its own; the pipeline is company-specific enough to watch, with the first named launch or approval as the milestone, and no disqualifier applies.

label: BDL
rationale: The Thales STARStreak teaming agreement is company-specific and credible, but it carries no order value or quantity, so it is not firm and size against trailing revenue of Rs 2,252 cr is unknown. The Aero India launches and MoUs have no stated value. The margin gain has no identified operating event and does not qualify on its own. The milestone that would make this firm is a signed production or supply contract with a stated value.

label: HCL-INSYS
rationale: The Rs 303.35 crore disposal proceeds are stated and completed, 56.5% of TTM revenue (537.00 crore). It is a one-off divestment that repays debt, not an operating step-up, and the completion already falls within the reported Dec-quarter results. The company is stressed: TTM PAT is -225.83 crore, debt is high and an equity subscription was needed. The sale does not restore earnings. Reject.

label: UMIYA-MRO
rationale: Size cannot be estimated: the only order disclosure is a generic sentence with no value, counterparty or LOA, against TTM revenue of 28.53 crore. The company is loss-making (TTM PAT -9.92 crore), with finance cost of about 1.3-1.5 crore a quarter against quarterly revenue of 6-11 crore, and is illiquid; this is a STRESSED profile. The order claim is recorded as the milestone to watch for, but no deep research.

label: GLENMARK
rationale: The US approvals (169 marketed products, 42-43 ANDAs pending) and the sunitinib generic launch are Glenmark's regular generic flow, not a step-change for a company with Rs 10,852 crore TTM revenue. The packet's 3,360.37 million 'firm order' is Q3 regional revenue for Africa, Asia and CIS, so it is not an order. The margin gain has no stated operating cause beyond routine approvals.

label: VASCONEQ
rationale: The new firm order of 38 crore is stated and equals about 8.5% of TTM revenue of 445.37 crore, below the 10% threshold. The 69 crore figure is a year-to-date total that includes it, and the 150 crore metro item is non-binding. The company is stressed, with TTM PAT of -43.78 crore and gross debt of about 233 crore, so it is unlikely to capture the benefit. The debt reduction is a financing change and not an operating earnings change.

label: UFLEX
rationale: The Poland BOPET line is commissioned, so it is firm, and the combined 63,000 TPA addition (including the UAE proposal) at 50% year-one utilisation and an assumed INR 1.5 lakh per tonne is about INR 473 crore, roughly 5.8% of TTM revenue of INR 8,088 crore. That is below the 10% threshold and is in line with UFlex's regular capacity additions, so it is routine. The profit surge is already in reported results and partly reflects pandemic-era packaging demand, so there is no deep research case.

label: BHEL
rationale: The Navy gun-mount order is firm but estimated at under 1% of TTM revenue of Rs 15,188 crore even at a generous Rs 100 crore for two mounts, so it is immaterial. The 800 MW commissioning is routine project completion for BHEL, and the SRU bid is L-1 and the partnerships are MoUs, so none is firm. Trailing losses of Rs 3,196 crore make the company stressed, which is a disqualifier on its own.

label: ALKEM
rationale: The six EIRs are regulatory outcomes already received, but they date from 2016 to May 2020 and the investor presentation and results only restate them, so the item is already in reported results and is not a new change. The 205 bps margin rise and 23 percent finance-cost fall are not tied to any new event in the packet. Alkem is profitable (TTM PAT 1,560 cr), so no stress disqualifier applies; a new classification or disclosed US sales uplift would need to appear before this is revisited.

label: TATACONSUM
rationale: The product launches are unquantified line extensions in a Rs 10,970 cr trailing revenue base, so they are routine. The operating profit gain is coupled with a 56.5% revenue jump and a 46.0% rise in share count, which points to a structural change the packet does not explain rather than a specific operating event. Size is unknown and no disqualifier applies; the rejection rests on the packet not establishing an operating mechanism.

label: KHADIM
