Rejected: routine flow, unquantifiable, and a results-highlights noise item; no deep research.

label: CRISIL
rationale: The only trigger is the ICON platform launch, with no disclosed value, client count or demand, so it is not shown to be firm. Even if ICON were the whole Advisory segment (Rs 134.1 cr of 2020 income, 6.8% of trailing revenue of Rs 1,981.83 cr), it could not reach the 10% threshold, so it is immaterial on the packet's own numbers. The operating-profit rise has no identified mechanism and is not evidence of an inflection.

label: ACC
rationale: Estimated at 50% utilisation and Rs 3,500 per tonne, the commissioned Sindri unit (1.4 MTPA, about Rs 245 crore a year, 1.8% of TTM revenue of Rs 13,786 crore) and the Ametha plan (2.7 MTPA, about 3.4%) together come to about 5%, far below 10% and routine capacity addition for a cement company. The only order is a related-party supply agreement with Ambuja Cements, which is internal demand. The margin and finance-cost gains are a financial change with no operating explanation.

label: JAYSREETEA
rationale: The Rs 50 crore debt reduction is about 6.4% of TTM revenue of 782.24 crore (19.2% if the 150 crore reading is correct), but it is a financial deleveraging via asset sales with no operating driver. The company is loss making (TTM PAT -25.94 crore) and carries debt, so it is stressed and unlikely to capture any benefit, which is a disqualifier. Rejected.

label: AARVI
rationale: The 53 crore order is stated and is about 24.8% of TTM revenue of INR 213.46 crore; no execution period is given, so the stated total is used. It is firm as a won order and not routine on the packet's disclosures, since it is the largest order disclosed and 1.7x the next-largest in the quarter. The same quarter also shows 30.69 crore and 8.2 crore wins and 10+ new contracts, so routine flow is a real risk, which is why confidence is low.

label: ZYDUSLIFE
rationale: Size is unknown: no approval states a value or quantity, against TTM revenue of INR 15,007.60 crore. The USFDA approvals are firm, but three approvals in five weeks (23 Jan, 19 Feb, 25 Feb 2021) are the company's ordinary generic launch flow, so they are routine. The Cyprium asset is unapproved (AMBITION) and a rare-disease product would need about INR 1,500 crore a year to reach 10% of revenue, and the finance cost drop has no operating explanation.

label: KANSAINER
rationale: Size is unknown: no revenue or volume is disclosed for the three launched products, against TTM revenue of INR 4,695 cr. The launches are in commercial operation, but three decorative product refreshes are normal flow for a paint company, and the packet's Q3 profit rise sits alongside 19.6% YoY revenue growth, which points to demand recovery rather than a change in trajectory. No disqualifier is assigned, and the company is funded (TTM PAT INR 467 cr), so the event is rejected as routine.

label: ADVENZYMES
rationale: The only operating catalyst is a non-binding management ceiling that the expanded SSPL business could reach about Rs 100 crore of revenue, roughly 21% of trailing group revenue of Rs 478.9 crore if achieved, which would clear the size test. It is not firm, so it is watch-only until the expansion is approved or commissioned and audited revenue is disclosed. The Rs 16 crore debt repayment and margin and finance-cost gains are financial changes and do not qualify on their own.

label: INE674A01014
rationale: A stated net debt reduction of Rs 495 crore exists in the investor presentation, but the packet has no revenue, so size cannot be expressed against revenue. Tradeability is unverified (no symbol, no prices), the source of the reduction is truncated, and the counterparty field is corrupted. Repair the packet before triage.

label: REPCOHOME
rationale: The event is a debt redemption of Rs 272 crore, about 19.6% of trailing four-quarter revenue of 1,385.91 crore, so it is sized and completed. It is a balance-sheet financial change, not an operating event; any interest saving is a financial effect with no operating explanation in the packet. Per the rules, a financial change with no operating explanation is rejected, and the finance cost check could not be verified.

label: SALZERELEC
rationale: The secured Australia/New Zealand contract is firm on management's statement and is non-routine because the company had not served that market, but it has no stated value. The only stated value, USD 4-5 million of additional export business with no period, is about 5.8 percent of TTM revenue (Rs 568 crore) at an assumed Rs 73.5 per USD, which is below the 10 percent threshold. The wire harness ramp is operating but largely already in reported results, and the price pass-through is not an inflection. Watch for the contract value and first revenue in Q1 FY22.

label: INE676A01019
rationale: Stated contract values sum to more than US$64 mn over 2 to 6 year periods, but the packet has no revenue or financial snapshot, so the percentage of revenue is not computed. The wins are several similar managed-services and data-centre deals in one quarter's highlights, which is routine flow for an IT services business. No disqualifier is shown, but the packet's name and symbol data do not establish that the security still trades and should be repaired before any later research.

label: INDIANHUME
rationale: The stated Rs 162.23 cr is 13.75% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,179.66 cr, but it is only an L1 position, so it is not firm. The order book of Rs 4,691.57 cr is about four times TTM revenue and grew by about Rs 1,030 cr in the year, so annual order inflow is a multiple of revenue and a project of this size is the company's normal flow, which makes it routine. REJECT_WITH_REASON.

label: SADBHIN
rationale: Provisional COD on unnamed road projects is a firm operating start, but no value or quantity is given, so size against revenue is unknown. The company is stressed: losses in every quarter except the Mar-2020 quarter (which was flattered by an exceptional gain), finance costs of INR 211-345 crore a quarter, a debt restructuring, and new debentures to repay debt. The fix needed is financing, not the projects, so the STRESSED disqualifier applies.

label: AURIONPRO
rationale: The release describes a bank selection and the exchange filing calls it an order, which we treat as firm, but it states no value, term or rollout scope, so size against revenue is unknown (TTM revenue about Rs 369 crore). Whether it is more than the company's usual flow is not established from the packet, and the Q3 margin expansion predates this announcement and is not explained by it. Watch for a disclosed contract value or rollout scope before any deep research; no disqualifier applies, and the thin trading liquidity is not one.

label: CHAMBLFERT
rationale: The trigger is a government subsidy allocation that reduces debt and finance cost, which is a financial change rather than an operating one. The quarterly finance cost saving of about Rs 57 cr is an annualised effect of roughly 1.7% of trailing revenue of Rs 13,047 cr, below the 10% threshold, and the amount of the allocation is not stated in the packet. The margin gain has no identified operating mechanism, so no inflection is shown.

label: RPPINFRA
rationale: The 174.03 crore order is a firm award to RPP's 49% JV; RPP's share (about INR 85 crore) is 17.3% of TTM revenue of INR 492.44 crore, above the 10% line. It is the first firm order disclosed in the packet, so it is not routine on this evidence, though the later 157.87 and 176.58 crore orders are similar in size and their routine status is untested. The company is profitable, so the rights issue is a funding question rather than a stress disqualifier.

label: ESTER
rationale: The new product line has started commercial sales, which counts as firm, and a new product line is not routine. Its size is unknown: the packet gives no product revenue, no volume and no trailing annual revenue, so it cannot be placed against the 10 percent threshold, and the most this allows is watch. The 26.8 crore debt repayment is a balance-sheet event and is rejected under 3.3 as a financial change, and the INR 587 crore capex is non-binding and not firm.

label: BLIL
rationale: The only trigger passage is OCR-garbled text that the page-6 read shows to be a labour-code and gratuity disclosure, not an order, so the event is noise and a fatal flaw. There is no order value or quantity, and the packet has no financials to size against. Nothing in the packet shows a change from business as usual.

label: PNCINFRA
rationale: The INR 881 crore COD is 16.7 percent of TTM revenue of INR 5,270 crore, and the six EPC awards are firm. A road EPC contractor that completes projects and wins several EPC contracts at a time is business as usual, so the event is routine rather than a change in trajectory. The margin and profit gains are a COVID-recovery base effect with a weak operating link to the awards, so there is no deep-research case.

label: EVEREADY
rationale: Size is unknown: the only commercial item is an unquantified battery and flashlight price increase to offset rupee depreciation, and no value or quantity is given. It is not firm and not a change from business as usual: page 14 attributes the margin gain (11.3% to 20.1%) to mix, lower distribution, promotional and overhead spend during COVID restrictions, and currency pass-through pricing. These effects are temporary or cyclical and already in reported Q3 results, so the financial change has an operating explanation that does not indicate a trajectory change. Rejected.

label: APARINDS
rationale: The 450 crore order is firm and stated and equals about 7.1% of TTM revenue of 6,302.33 crore, below the 10% threshold. The packet has no earlier order history, so routine status cannot be tested, and nothing in it shows a path from this order to material revenue. The capacity item is a management expectation, and the margin and operating-profit rise in the Dec 2020 quarter has no identified mechanism and predates the order.

label: TMPV
rationale: The list-price increase is in effect, but a price revision across a passenger-vehicle range is ordinary commercial action, and no volume is given to size it against FY2020 revenue of Rs 261,068 crore. The Q3 margin gain precedes the announcement, so the packet offers no operating explanation for it. The awards mention is not a launch, so the trigger set adds no inflection; rejected as routine pricing and an unexplained margin move.

label: RUPA
rationale: A premium-brand launch is a credible, company-specific candidate for a 370 bps margin gain, but the pages read give no premium-brand sales or margin and the launches read as ongoing strategy, so nothing is firm. Quarterly revenue grew only 5-12%, so the margin gain is not tied to a material revenue line and size is unknown. Watch for disclosure of premium-brand sales.

label: APEX
rationale: The trigger describes moving existing processing from a leased facility to a new plant, with no added capacity, product or customer stated, so it is not a revenue step-change. No value or quantity is given, so size against TTM revenue of INR 777 crore is unknown. The December-quarter profit fall runs against any upside, so reject as routine operations.

label: ZENTEC
rationale: The trigger is a finance cost drop (Rs 0.17 cr in the latest quarter) and a gross margin rise, both with no operating event; the packet attributes the debt reduction to equity raised in the lookback, which is financing, not earnings. Revenue is falling sharply, so there is no operating inflection in the packet. No event value exists, size is unknown, and nothing is firm, so this is REJECT_WITH_REASON for a financial change with no operating explanation.

label: TIMETECHNO
rationale: The recorded value of Rs 809 crore is the total debt level, about 27.2% of TTM revenue of 2,969.87 crore, but the passage shows the actual reduction was about Rs 23 crore (roughly 0.8% of TTM revenue). A small debt reduction with no operating explanation is a financial change, so it is rejected.

label: AMBUJACEM
rationale: The grinding unit is commissioned, so it is firm, but at 1.4 MTPA the estimated value (INR 280 cr at 50% utilisation and an assumed INR 4,000 per tonne) is about 1.1% of trailing revenue of INR 24,516 cr, which is immaterial with no plausible path to 10%. The ACC master supply agreement is an intra-group renewal on unchanged terms, which is internal demand and not an inflection. The margin and finance-cost moves are explained in part by the special-products mix and cost savings, so the case is rejected.

label: DYNAMATECH
rationale: The change is a board-approved refinancing that lowers interest cost, which is a financial change with no operating explanation. Its size is not stated, and the finance cost fall is modest relative to trailing revenue of Rs 1,138 cr. Reject as an immaterial financial change; the separate JKM Ferrotech asset sale is not sized in the packet.

label: NACLIND
rationale: Commercial production of two new granular formulations is firm and a new product line is not routine, but the packet gives no value and no demand evidence, so size against TTM revenue of INR 1,138 crore is unknown. The promoter loan repayment is financing under 3.3 and is not an operating event. The margin gain has no operating explanation in the packet beyond the launches, so the milestone is revenue disclosure from the new formulations.

label: PENINLAND
rationale: Size is stated: Rs 430 crore against TTM revenue of 481.15 crore (89.4%), and the reduction is firm (pledge invoked July 2020). It is disqualified as stressed: the company is loss-making (TTM PAT -260.29 crore), its NCDs were enforced by a debenture trustee, and the debt cut came from losing a subsidiary investment rather than from earnings. The event does not restore the earnings base.

label: INE222J01013
rationale: The deck states three secured orders worth INR 86 crore a year in total, but with no revenue base the size against revenue cannot be computed. The identical three lines appear in four Rane group filings, so it is not clear which entity holds them, and no exchange symbol or price is on record. The company cannot be established as a listed, reporting business from this packet, so the case needs data repair before any triage judgment.

label: MONTECARLO
rationale: The trigger value of Rs 1,472 million (147.2 crore, 23.6% of standalone TTM revenue of 622.72 crore) is a cash balance in the investor presentation, not a debt repayment; the same slide shows long-term borrowing of only Rs 128.7 million. The event is a misread and a fatal flaw. No change to earnings is evidenced, and the margin and finance cost moves have no stated operating explanation.

label: TATAPOWER
rationale: The NESCO item is a conditional letter of intent, so it is not firm; the milestone is the final OERC licence. Size is estimated from the 5,450 MU input energy at an assumed INR 4.0/kWh, about INR 2,180 cr or 7.5% of TTM revenue (28,961.51 cr), which is below 10% even if firm, so the outcome is watch. It would be a new distribution revenue line, so it is not routine. The 4,150 cr bank-loan repayment is a financial change with no operating event and is rejected; the solar awards are firm but routine.

label: MARKSANS
rationale: Gross margin rose 925 bps and operating profit 92.6% YoY on TTM revenue of INR 1,381.33 cr and TTM PAT of INR 201.78 cr, so the financial change is real. The only stated operating cause is an unnamed launch and a generic UK/USA pipeline with no product, size or timing, so nothing is firm and size cannot be stated. Debt repayment is a financial change and does not qualify on its own; the pipeline is company-specific enough to watch, with the first named launch or approval as the milestone, and no disqualifier applies.

label: BDL
rationale: The Thales STARStreak teaming agreement is company-specific and credible, but it carries no order value or quantity, so it is not firm and size against trailing revenue of Rs 2,252 cr is unknown. The Aero India launches and MoUs have no stated value. The margin gain has no identified operating event and does not qualify on its own. The milestone that would make this firm is a signed production or supply contract with a stated value.

label: HCL-INSYS
rationale: The Rs 303.35 crore disposal proceeds are stated and completed, 56.5% of TTM revenue (537.00 crore). It is a one-off divestment that repays debt, not an operating step-up, and the completion already falls within the reported Dec-quarter results. The company is stressed: TTM PAT is -225.83 crore, debt is high and an equity subscription was needed. The sale does not restore earnings. Reject.

label: UMIYA-MRO
rationale: Size cannot be estimated: the only order disclosure is a generic sentence with no value, counterparty or LOA, against TTM revenue of 28.53 crore. The company is loss-making (TTM PAT -9.92 crore), with finance cost of about 1.3-1.5 crore a quarter against quarterly revenue of 6-11 crore, and is illiquid; this is a STRESSED profile. The order claim is recorded as the milestone to watch for, but no deep research.

label: KERNEX
rationale: Size is unknown: no commercial event or value is identified, and the margin move sits on a TTM revenue base of only INR 5.00 crore, so it is immaterial. The margin jump has no operating explanation in the packet, and revenue up 153.5% is flagged for possible reclassification. The equity raise is the only reported event and its use is not stated, so this is a financial change with no operating explanation.

label: GLENMARK
rationale: The US approvals (169 marketed products, 42-43 ANDAs pending) and the sunitinib generic launch are Glenmark's regular generic flow, not a step-change for a company with Rs 10,852 crore TTM revenue. The packet's 3,360.37 million 'firm order' is Q3 regional revenue for Africa, Asia and CIS, so it is not an order. The margin gain has no stated operating cause beyond routine approvals.

label: VASCONEQ
rationale: The new firm order of 38 crore is stated and equals about 8.5% of TTM revenue of 445.37 crore, below the 10% threshold. The 69 crore figure is a year-to-date total that includes it, and the 150 crore metro item is non-binding. The company is stressed, with TTM PAT of -43.78 crore and gross debt of about 233 crore, so it is unlikely to capture the benefit. The debt reduction is a financing change and not an operating earnings change.

label: UFLEX
rationale: The Poland BOPET line is commissioned, so it is firm, and the combined 63,000 TPA addition (including the UAE proposal) at 50% year-one utilisation and an assumed INR 1.5 lakh per tonne is about INR 473 crore, roughly 5.8% of TTM revenue of INR 8,088 crore. That is below the 10% threshold and is in line with UFlex's regular capacity additions, so it is routine. The profit surge is already in reported results and partly reflects pandemic-era packaging demand, so there is no deep research case.

label: BHEL
rationale: The Navy gun-mount order is firm but estimated at under 1% of TTM revenue of Rs 15,188 crore even at a generous Rs 100 crore for two mounts, so it is immaterial. The 800 MW commissioning is routine project completion for BHEL, and the SRU bid is L-1 and the partnerships are MoUs, so none is firm. Trailing losses of Rs 3,196 crore make the company stressed, which is a disqualifier on its own.

label: ALKEM
rationale: The six EIRs are regulatory outcomes already received, but they date from 2016 to May 2020 and the investor presentation and results only restate them, so the item is already in reported results and is not a new change. The 205 bps margin rise and 23 percent finance-cost fall are not tied to any new event in the packet. Alkem is profitable (TTM PAT 1,560 cr), so no stress disqualifier applies; a new classification or disclosed US sales uplift would need to appear before this is revisited.

label: INE140A01024
rationale: Size: the stated Rs 24,000 cr net-debt reduction is about 191% of annualised 9M revenue of about Rs 12,544 cr, but it is balance-sheet deleveraging funded by capital raising, not an operating change, so it is a financial change with no operating explanation. The launches (15+ products a year) and contract wins are routine, and the USD 32 mn expansion is capex with no timing. Operating trajectory is normal: 9M net profit up 12% and Q3 up 10% year on year, with CDMO revenue up 16%. The DHFL plan is the only possible step-change, but it is not a trigger and is a plan whose approval status is not in the packet, so it is not a basis for a pick; rejected.

label: TATACONSUM
rationale: The product launches are unquantified line extensions in a Rs 10,970 cr trailing revenue base, so they are routine. The operating profit gain is coupled with a 56.5% revenue jump and a 46.0% rise in share count, which points to a structural change the packet does not explain rather than a specific operating event. Size is unknown and no disqualifier applies; the rejection rests on the packet not establishing an operating mechanism.

label: KHADIM
rationale: The festive sub-brand launch is a commercial start, but the packet gives no value, volume or demand evidence, so size against TTM revenue of INR 514.44 cr is unknown. A festive-season line launch with no demand evidence is not a step-change in the business. The margin and finance-cost moves have no identified operating cause, and TTM PAT is a loss of INR 64.34 cr, so the case is rejected.

label: PSPPROJECT
rationale: The binding work order of INR 236 crore incl. GST (about INR 200 crore ex-GST at an assumed 18 percent GST) is firm and equals 16.7 percent of TTM revenue of INR 1,197 crore, above the 10 percent bar. Routine status is the main open question: management's normal inflow target of INR 1,300 to 1,500 crore a year suggests orders of this scale recur, but the single order exceeds the company's entire nine-month FY21 inflow of INR 221 crore, so the packet does not establish a routine pattern. The INR 588.62 crore LoI and the L1 ranking are not firm and are watch items; no disqualifier applies (TTM PAT INR 74 crore, INR 195 crore of deposits).

label: INOXWIND
rationale: Firm order for 62 MW of turnkey wind projects; at an assumed INR 4.0 crore per MW this is about INR 248 crore, roughly 37% of trailing revenue of INR 661 crore. The order would otherwise be non-routine against the 18 MW the packet shows as recently commissioned, but the company is stressed: trailing PAT of INR -393 crore, trailing finance cost of about INR 290 crore, and an NCLT-driven promoter change with new share allotments. The order does not by itself fix these losses, so the stressed disqualifier applies.

label: JSL
rationale: The Rs890 crore debt reduction is firm but equals about 7.8% of trailing-four-quarter revenue of Rs11,368.93 crore, below the 10% threshold. It is a financial change with no operating explanation, and the margin and operating profit gains are unexplained in the packet. Rejected as a financial change without an identified operating trigger.

label: KEC
rationale: Size: the stated Rs 1,681 cr order is 13.5% of TTM revenue of Rs 12,425 cr (the Rs 1,140 cr release is 9.2%), and both are binding orders, so they are firm. Routine: KEC is an EPC company whose order inflow runs at multiples of revenue, with three releases of Rs 1,000 cr or more in about seven weeks (10 Jan, 16 Feb and 28 Feb 2021), so these are its normal flow and not an inflection. The order book and TTM inflow are not in the packet, but the company's stated pattern of order wins is enough to reject as routine; no disqualifier applies, and funding is not an issue given TTM PAT of Rs 551 cr.

label: ESCORTS
rationale: Size is unknown because the price-increase magnitude is not clearly stated, against TTM revenue of INR 6,171 cr. The pricing is implemented, but it is the company's ordinary price and cost response in a cyclical revenue recovery, and its margin effect (486 bps, operating profit up 70%) is already in reported Q3 results rather than ahead of them. No disqualifier applies (TTM PAT INR 734 cr), so the event is rejected as routine.

label: JINDALSAW
rationale: Size is unknown: the only trigger is an unquantified statement of received and expected oil and gas orders with no counterparty. Pipe orders are the company's normal business, and the packet shows no specific award, so the statement is not credible enough to show a change from business as usual. The margin move is not attributed to any order. Reject for now; revisit only if a quantified award is announced.

label: GVT&D
rationale: The Power Grid packages total about Rs 300 crore, which is 9.3% of TTM revenue of Rs 3,212 crore and below the 10% threshold. Most of the value is L1, not firm, and transformer and reactor packages from utilities are the company's ordinary order flow, so the orders are routine. The margin turnaround and debt reduction have only management commentary as explanation in the packet, and the packet's tagging of the Rs 49 billion backlog as debt reduction is wrong; no disqualifier applies. Rejected as routine and below the materiality threshold.

label: APLLTD
rationale: USFDA final approval is received, so the event is firm. Size is unknown: the packet gives no value or quantity, and against TTM revenue of Rs 5,319.57 crore no percentage can be stated. The first injectable ANDA, among 138 total approvals, opens a new dosage-form line, so it is non-routine; with size unknown this is WATCH_MILESTONE, and the test is the first launch or sales disclosure. No disqualifier applies.

label: PRINCEPIPE
rationale: Phase one is 4,020 t/yr of installed capacity; at 50% utilisation and an assumed INR 1.2 lakh/t (low end), that is about INR 24 crore, or 1.4% of TTM revenue of INR 1,740.92 crore. Commercial production makes it firm and a seventh plant in a new region is non-routine, but phase one is below 10%. The full 50,000 t plan gives about 17% at 50% utilisation over 2 to 3 years, which is the plausible path to material, so watch for disclosed volumes and phase-two commissioning.

label: JASH
rationale: The stated INR 15 crore for three Indian desalination projects is about 5.8% of TTM revenue of INR 258.6 crore, below 10%. The investor presentation calls it negotiated, not a received order, while the call says the company 'bagged' the orders, so firmness is ambiguous and is treated as not firm. If firmed, desalination in India would be a new market for the company and so non-routine; the watch trigger is a named purchase order or letter of award.

label: RANEHOLDIN
rationale: The three firm orders total INR 86 crore a year, 4.6 percent of trailing revenue of INR 1,859 crore, and each line is only 1.4 to 1.7 percent, so the size is below the 10 percent threshold. They fall within the normal product lines of an auto component group, and the packet shows no step-change. Immaterial and routine, so rejected.

label: NTPC
rationale: Size is estimated at about 0.9% of TTM revenue of INR 111,629.63 crore (Gadarwara 800 MW x 8,760 h x 50% x INR 3.00/kWh = about INR 1,051 crore). The capacity is firm (commissioned or declared commercial), but NTPC declared about six units or plants in five weeks in this period, so the additions are routine commissioning rather than a step-change. The 264 bps gross margin move has no operating mechanism in the packet, and the event is immaterial to earnings.

label: BEML
rationale: The 576-car MMRDA metro order has no stated value, so it is estimated as 576 cars x an assumed INR 3 crore per car = INR 1,728 cr, or 60.7% of TTM revenue of INR 2,847.84 cr in total over about three years to January 2024. It is a received order from an external government body, and the company calls it its largest ever with no earlier comparable order in the packet, so it is not routine; the company's order book above INR 12,000 cr is the main counterpoint. A firm MoD order of about INR 758 cr (26.6% of revenue, stated) supports the change, and no stress or other disqualifier applies on TTM profitability and funding.

label: BUTTERFLY
rationale: Size: the stated 90 crore order is 11.6% of trailing four quarters' revenue of 774.06 crore. It is firm, but routine: the same presentation reports a 4th TNCSC order, so repeated government supply orders of this kind are part of the company's normal flow. The revenue step-up is already visible in the Sep and Dec 2020 quarters, and the debt reduction and equity raise are financing events, not operating inflections.

label: ADANIENT
rationale: Size cannot be estimated: the NHAI LOA states no value or length, against TTM revenue of 39,440.89 crore. It is firm, but routine: the packet shows five NHAI hybrid-annuity concessions already signed, and this is one more road award in that flow. The margin change is group-level and not tied to this order, so there is no operating inflection.

label: CARYSIL
rationale: Firm: commercial production of 100,000 additional units began 25 Feb 2021, so the capacity is commissioned. Size: the packet has no annual revenue, so the base is the quarter ending Dec 2020 (Rs 87.48 cr) annualised to about Rs 350 cr; estimated 50% year-one utilisation x Rs 2,000 per unit (low end of the usual range) gives about Rs 10 cr, or 2.9% of revenue, and 5.7% even at full utilisation. The volume is a roughly 17% same-product capacity step on the stated 600,000-unit base, not a new revenue line, and the TekCarysil brand launch has no demand evidence. Immaterial on the conservative estimate, so rejected.

label: GREENPANEL
rationale: Size: 110,000 cbm added x 50% first-year utilisation = 55,000 cbm, x Rs 12,000/cbm (assumed low end) = Rs 66 crore, or 7.6% of TTM revenue of Rs 869.73 crore. The capex is announced with dated completion but is not commissioned, so not firm; it is company-specific and capacity-led, so watch the Nov-Dec 2021 commissioning. The price rises are firm but are cost pass-through (business as usual), and the net debt cut is financial, so neither qualifies on its own.

label: PURVA
rationale: The Rs 221 crore debt reduction, though firm and funded by equity, is a balance-sheet and financial change; rule 1 does not size it on the balance sheet and it has no revenue. No operating event (order, commissioning, new project) appears in the packet, and the gross margin rise has no commercial explanation while revenue fell 50% to 71%. Reject as a financial change with no operating explanation.

label: DWARKESH
rationale: Estimated at about 4.8% of trailing revenue of Rs1,700.63 crore (100 KLPD x 365 days x 50% utilisation x an assumed Rs45 per litre, about Rs82 crore), even if fully realised, so below the 10% threshold. It is a management-stated plan with no timeline or funding, and debottlenecking an existing distillery is routine capacity work. Rejected as immaterial, though the Dec 2020 operating profit rise is unexplained and could be revisited if a commercial mechanism is evidenced.

label: JKIL
rationale: The MMRDA order is firm and stated at INR 1,998 crore, about 81.3% of TTM revenue of INR 2,456.63 crore (67% of FY20 revenue), well above the 10% line. It is not routine on the packet: it is about 30% larger than the NHAI INR 1,540 crore order in the company's own milestone slide and far above a normal 20 to 40% order, although that comparable makes the routine test contestable. Trailing PAT is positive and management calls the company almost net debt free, so there is no stress disqualifier.

label: ONMOBILE
rationale: Size is unknown: the AI and cloud products are in beta with no revenue, value or quantity disclosed, against TTM revenue of INR 567 cr. The only disclosure is a presentation slide, which is a plan rather than a commitment and so not firm; the product investment is ongoing flow for a company that has been investing in digital products. The margin and operating-profit rise is on revenue down 2.4% YoY and is not linked to these products, so the financial change has no operating explanation and the event is rejected.

label: TRIVENI
rationale: Size estimated at 7.9%: 9.86 crore litres x an assumed INR 40 per litre gives INR 394.4 crore, against TTM revenue of 5,009.30 crore; the packet's stated figure misreads litres as rupees. The contracts are firm, but they are the company's annual ethanol supply-year allocation, so they are routine. Below the 10% threshold, and the margin and finance-cost changes have no operating mechanism in the packet.

label: HATSUN
rationale: Size: 6 LLPD x 365 days x 50% year-one utilisation = 10.95 crore litres; at an assumed conservative Rs 30 per litre realisation (low end of the usual milk-equivalent price), that is about Rs 329 cr, or 6.2% of TTM revenue of Rs 5,267 cr (about 12.5% at full utilisation). Firmness: commercial production has started, so the capacity is firm. Routine: the company commissioned the Udhiyur paneer plant on 27 Jan 2021 and has a 1.5 LLPD unit flagged for Mar 2021, so dairy plant starts are a regular flow of similar additions; with no disqualifier it is rejected as routine and below 10% in year one, though the full-utilisation path is noted.

label: BAJAJELEC
rationale: The price hike of 5-8% is stated and effective 1 Jan, so it is firm, but a routine cost pass-through on a business with steady sales is business as usual, and the 5% low end is below the 10% test. The profit jump is largely a low-base COVID recovery plus lower finance cost from debt repayment, which is a financial change with no new operating explanation. Debt reduction is funding, not an earnings inflection.

label: SANGHVIMOV
rationale: The only change is a lower finance cost from debt repayment, which has no operating explanation. Annualised, the Rs 3.8 cr quarterly saving is small against trailing revenue of Rs 218 cr. Reject as a financial change with no operating explanation.

label: LUXIND
rationale: Size is unknown: the trigger is a debt reduction with no stated value, and the revenue and margin gains are not tied to any order or contract. This is business as usual for an innerwear company (volume, mix and cost trends), and the results are already fully in the 12 February release (page 2 to 3), so the disqualifier is FATAL_FLAW. The margin driver is an operating explanation, but it is an ongoing trend rather than a new event. Rejected.

label: LASA
rationale: The packet has no financials, so size against revenue is unknown. The only disclosed change is a 95.40% fall in finance cost and a 154% rise in PAT, which is a financial change with no operating explanation. Rejected as a financial change without an identified operating trigger, with low confidence given the thin packet.

label: NEULANDLAB
rationale: Commercial production at Unit 3 with active API shipments is firm and opens a new output stream, so it is not routine. Neither the packet nor the cited filing page states a value, capacity or quantity for it, so size against TTM revenue of INR 883.85 crore is unknown and cannot be placed against the 10 percent threshold. The Q3 operating profit gain is partly already in reported results, so the milestone is revenue or volume disclosure from Unit 3 over the following quarters.

label: MARINE
rationale: The Rs 6 crore Nagpur Metro order is firm, and it opens a metro-rail segment that is new for the company, so it is not routine. It is immaterial: Rs 6 crore is about 2.2% of annualized revenue (Dec-2020 quarter Rs 67.43 crore x 4 = Rs 269.7 crore), and the packet shows no pipeline large enough to close the gap to the 10% threshold. Rejected as immaterial; no disqualifier.

label: IDEA
rationale: The brand relaunch dates from September 2020, so it is already in reported results and is not a new revenue stream. The company has TTM PAT of INR -48,854 cr and quarterly finance cost of about INR 4,787 cr, so the heavy-losses-plus-high-debt STRESSED disqualifier applies; the board-approved fundraise is a plan, not yet the fix. The operating margin improvement is real but does not change the balance-sheet picture.

label: BRIGADE
rationale: The stated Rs 140 crore repayment is 7.8% of TTM revenue (1,794.65 crore), below the 10% threshold. It comes from ordinary collections swept to repay loans, which is routine cash flow rather than a step change, and the 2-3% January price increase is a normal move. There is no new order or revenue stream, and the gross margin figure is unexplained. Not an inflection.

label: BODALCHEM
rationale: The Trion plant is firmly commercial (production since September 2020), but at about 230 MT per month and near breakeven its annual value is roughly INR 28 crore on an assumed INR 1 lakh per tonne, about 2.4% of TTM revenue of INR 1,162 crore, so it is immaterial. The margin and finance-cost gains are already in the reported Q3FY21 results, which is a disqualifier under the fatal-flaw rule. No deep research.

label: SALASAR
rationale: The Rs 252 cr is a signed work contract (presentation page 7), not an L1 bid, so it is firm and equals about 51% of trailing revenue of Rs 493.7 cr. The packet shows no earlier comparable order and the metro ballastless-track scope is new to the disclosed segments, so not routine on the available evidence. Trailing PAT is positive at Rs 23.8 cr and debt is not shown as stressed, so no disqualifier; contract terms and the Texmaco pass-through are the main open questions.

label: POWERGRID
legal_name: Power Grid Corporation of India Limited
rationale: A TBCB successful-bidder letter of intent is not a firm award, and the packet gives no project value, so size is unknown. POWERGRID already disclosed an earlier LoI on 29 Jan 2021, so transmission bid wins are its regular flow rather than a change in trajectory. Nothing in the packet marks this as a non-routine step.

label: EKC
rationale: The Rs 45 crore Aurangabad capacity plan is a non-binding expansion (about 5% of TTM revenue of Rs 863.5 crore) with the first phase in FY24, so it is neither firm nor material. The hydrogen-cylinder item is a demand expectation, not an order. The profit and finance-cost gains are a financial change with no operating event in the packet.

label: GRASIM
rationale: The largest new-capacity item, UltraTech's 12.8 MTPA expansion, is board-approved and not firm. At 50% year-one utilisation and an assumed INR 3,500 per tonne it is about INR 2,240 crore, roughly 3% of TTM revenue of INR 72,909 crore, so it is immaterial to group earnings and is routine cement capacity planning. The debt reduction and margin and profit gains are already in reported Q3FY21 results with no new operating mechanism, so there is no deep research case.

label: PREMEXPLN
rationale: Firm MoD orders of Rs 34.1 cr (counted once) are 22% of trailing revenue of Rs 153.7 cr. They open new products and customers (flares and chaffs for MoD, the IAI 82H variant, VSSC PSOM-XL), and no earlier comparable order is in the packet, so not routine; the 9 Feb call's Rs 233 cr defence book means some defence flow pre-dated this, so the routine test is only partly closed. The company is loss-making (TTM PAT -Rs 15.9 cr) and debt is not in the packet, so the stressed disqualifier is not established.

label: RITES
rationale: The largest firm order is the KIIFB PMC award of INR 61.25 crore, about 3.4% of TTM revenue of INR 1,794 crore. RITES says it won more than 60 projects in Q3FY21, so these orders are routine flow rather than an inflection. The Haryana order is only L-1 and not firm, and the reported margin gain has no operating mechanism in the packet.

label: MOREPENLAB
rationale: The expansion is a board-approved plan with environmental clearance pending, so it is not firm. Estimated at about Rs 22 crore a year (2,000 MT x 50% utilisation x Rs 2.2 lakh/t, the lowest realisation implied by the packet), it is about 2% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,108.06 crore, and full use gives about 4%, well short of the 10% test. It is rejected as immaterial, though a much higher price for the new molecules is the only route to a larger effect.

label: GODREJCP
rationale: The change is a lower finance cost from routine debt repayment, which is a balance-sheet effect rather than an operating change. Annualising the Rs 23.7 cr quarterly drop gives roughly 0.9% of trailing revenue (Rs 10,452 cr), which is immaterial. The pricing move is routine. Reject: financial change with no operating explanation and immaterial.

label: GAYAPROJ
rationale: Size: the stated Rs 1,324 cr LoA is 38.4% of TTM revenue of Rs 3,451 cr (contract period not stated). Firmness: the 23 Feb 2021 LoA is received, so the award is firm. Routine: this is a road and irrigation EPC company whose order wins since Q3 FY21 (about Rs 3,468 cr since Q3 FY21) roughly equal a year's revenue, so a 20-40% order is its normal flow and not a change in trajectory. The debt reduction is from one-off claim and award inflows rather than operations, and no disqualifier is established, but the event is routine, so rejected.

label: VARROC
rationale: The EUR 41 million of re-wins is roughly INR 361 crore at an assumed INR 88 per EUR, about 3.5 percent of trailing revenue of INR 10,428 crore, and re-wins are routine for a tier-I auto component group. The fall in net debt to INR 2,730 crore is balance-sheet repair from cash flow, not a change in earnings. Heavy trailing losses (PAT -INR 621 crore) alongside high net debt meet the stressed-company disqualifier.

label: GENUSPOWER
rationale: Size: 10,000 gas meters x assumed Rs 2,000 per meter = Rs 2 crore, 0.3% of TTM revenue of Rs 665.46 crore (estimated from quantity). It is firm (order received), and gas metering is a new product line, so it is not routine. Management's market view (Rs 800-1,000 crore industry, at least 15% share, transcript page 5) would put the path above 10% of TTM revenue, but it is unfirm, so the milestone is conversion of the next order rather than deep research now.

label: SOLARINDS
rationale: Size is unknown: the order has no stated value and the three plants have no capacity quantity (the transcript says the project details are yet to be finalised), so the INR 210 crore and 180 crore capex figures cannot size revenue. Nothing is firm yet: the board has only approved a plan, and the order awaits bulk-production clearance, so it is conditional. The company is profitable (TTM PAT INR 246 crore) and the defence order is company-specific, so it goes on watch with clearance, first supply and disclosed plant capacity as the milestones.

label: COCHINSHIP
rationale: The estimated INR 10,000 crore is about 391% of trailing revenue of INR 2,555 crore, a step-change into a new naval vessel class. It is not firm because L1 status is not a letter of award or contract, so the milestone is a signed Navy contract for the six NGMV. The dredger MoU is non-binding and adds nothing firm; the company is profitable and the packet shows an equity raise, so it is not stressed.

label: GREENLAM
rationale: The product launches are unquantified and are line extensions within a Rs 1,108 cr trailing revenue base, which makes them routine rather than a new revenue stream. The margin gain and finance cost drop have no identified operating event, and the finance cost change is a financial item. Size is unknown and no disqualifier is needed to reject.

label: SOUTHWEST
rationale: The Rs 1 crore GSI letter of award is firm but about 1% of TTM revenue of Rs 102.7 crore, which is immaterial against the 10% test. It is a single small exploration job, so it cannot explain the Q3 revenue and profit jump, which remains unexplained by any event in the packet. The illiquid, sub-Rs 140 crore company gives no path to material earnings change from this award.

label: PRAJIND
rationale: The stated INR 226.90 cr binding order is 21.9 percent of trailing four-quarter revenue of INR 1,033.86 cr, above the 10 percent threshold. It is firm: a received order from an external customer, IOCL. No comparable earlier order is in the packet, so it is treated as non-routine on this evidence. No disqualifier applies; the company is profitable with negligible finance cost. The order postdates the Q3 quarter, so it cannot explain the Q3 margin gain; execution timing and order margin remain open.

label: MATRIMONY
rationale: The only trigger is a generic 'launched new products and services' line in the Q3 release, with no named product, customer or value, so there is nothing to size (TTM revenue 370.86 cr; size unknown). The margin and profit gains are in the Q3 results filed the same day, so they are already in reported results and the packet gives no operating cause. This is boilerplate rather than a specific change: FATAL_FLAW, no deep research.

label: THERMAX
rationale: Size estimated at about 0.13%: two boilers at an assumed INR 3 crore each give INR 6 crore against TTM revenue of 4,539.69 crore; the other items are unquantified. Boiler and energy-plant orders are the company's normal flow at this revenue base, and the 33 MW synchronisation is not a new revenue event in the packet. The margin gain is not tied to a specific order, so there is no inflection.

label: RAMCOCEM
rationale: Size: 1 MTPA grinding x 50% year-one utilisation x Rs 4,500/t = Rs 225 crore, 4.5% of TTM revenue of Rs 5,051.27 crore (about 9% at full run-rate), estimated from quantity. It is not firm: the Kurnool unit is a funded plan and not commissioned. The reported margin rise is mainly fuel and power cost, not capacity, so it does not yet qualify as an operating inflection. Watch Kurnool commissioning and disclosed volumes.

label: MOTHERSON
rationale: Size is unknown: no value is stated for the debt reduction, and the trigger is a balance-sheet event rather than an order or product. The profit rise is a financial change whose only disclosed driver is lower gross debt and finance cost; no operating mechanism is shown, and the Q3 FY20 base was pre-COVID so no low-base effect explains it. No firm order or new product exists. Rejected under the no-operating-explanation rule.

label: TCIFINANCE
rationale: A loan was repaid and pledged shares released, which is firm, but the company is a microcap (market cap about INR 8 cr) and its finance cost fell by about INR 0.5 cr a quarter with no operating event. Operating profit growth from INR 0.91 cr to 1.46 cr has no identified mechanism and the revenue jump is unexplained. The change is immaterial on the packet evidence and does not meet the earnings-inflection test.

label: CUPID
rationale: The UP order is firm but was INR 8.3 crore, 5.7% of TTM revenue of INR 145.41 crore, and was fully supplied and paid before the cutoff, so it is already in reported results (fatal flaw) and is immaterial. The concall says WHO/UNFPA orders are already recurring, so the channel is routine rather than a change in trajectory. Rejected: no deep research.

label: IGPL
rationale: Size: PA-4 53,000 TPA x 50% first-year utilisation = 26,500 t, x Rs 60/kg (assumed low end) = Rs 159 crore, or 16.4% of TTM revenue of Rs 967.73 crore. Commissioning on 29 Dec 2020 is firm and most of its output is not yet in reported results. It adds about 24% to existing capacity, a step-change on the packet evidence, so not routine; the 80,000 TPA greenfield (about Rs 600 crore, about three years) is a plan and is not sized. Deep research should test PA-4 utilisation and realisation and the greenfield funding.

label: GRANULES
rationale: The USFDA approval is firm regulatory approval, but the packet gives no value or quantity, so size against FY20 consolidated revenue of INR 2,598.65 cr is unknown. The filing itself calls it the fourth ANDA approval in the same potassium chloride basket, so it is routine flow for this generics business and not a step-change. Rejected as routine with unknown materiality.

label: BSE
rationale: The life-insurance launch is operating (premium intermediated since December 2020), but the whole JV has disclosed Rs 2.35 crore of premium to 31 January 2021, and BSE holds only 40% of it, so BSE's share is too small to matter (fatal flaw). Against TTM revenue of Rs 468.75 crore, the upper bound is about 0.5%. The operating-margin rise has no identified operating event, so it does not qualify.

label: BHARTIARTL
rationale: Airtel Ads is a new advertising revenue stream that the company says it has launched, so it is firm, company-specific and not routine. No value, volume or revenue target is disclosed and the packet gives no quantity to estimate from, so size against TTM revenue of about Rs 1 lakh crore is unknown and cannot be judged material. The Nxtra item is a non-binding MoU and the segment profit turn is unexplained, so neither is a trigger. Watch for disclosed Airtel Ads revenue.

label: SATIA
rationale: 12,000 t at the company-stated average realisation of Rs 55,000/t gives Rs 66.0 cr, or 11.1% of trailing revenue of Rs 594.70 cr (the lower-realisation case; the Rs 33 cr stated for the 5,000 t Chhattisgarh order would take the total to about 12%). The orders are awarded, so firm; the packet shows no earlier comparable order and the company presents institutional sales as a recent push, so not routine. Trailing PAT is positive at Rs 44.72 cr with low finance cost, so no stress disqualifier; the realisation gain is the main margin driver.

label: JUBLFOOD
rationale: A new brand in an existing biryani segment is a line extension within an existing segment and is routine, not a new revenue stream of the scale needed for the 10% test. Its revenue is not stated and the packet has no size measure, so it is immaterial on the evidence. The margin gain is attributed only to the launch with no disclosed mechanism, and no disqualifier is needed to reject.

label: INE624C01015
rationale: The packet's commercial-start event is station 1's 2015 PCOD, which is not a new change. Station 2 is the only forward item: it is not firm (a 'likely' completion by March 2021 after prior delays) and has no quantity or financials, so size is unknown. Watch for station 2 PCOD and its first revenue, and confirm the stock still trades before any research.

label: AUROPHARMA
rationale: The USFDA approvals and launches are routine flow for a company that gets approvals every quarter, so they are not triggers. The Rs 2,000-3,000 crore capex plan is company-specific but is management talk, not board-approved or contracted, so it is not firm. Capex cannot size the event and no revenue or capacity quantity is stated, so size is unknown; it is a watch case until board approval and a revenue-linked capacity disclosure appear.

label: DCAL
rationale: Size is unknown: the business update gives no value, volume or customer for the first commercial ADC campaign and no product quantity. It is company-specific and a step from validation toward commercial supply, so not routine, but no supply agreement or PO is disclosed, so not firm. Revenue fell 13.6% YoY in the December quarter and the margin driver is unexplained, so it goes on watch until a committed value appears.

label: CYIENT
rationale: Size is unknown because no investment amount, customer order or revenue is stated, against TTM revenue of INR 4,113 cr. The event is a customer-qualification and platform announcement with no firm order, and it is a product-level investment in an existing aerospace digitisation business rather than a change in trajectory. There is no plausible path to 10% of revenue from the packet alone, so it is rejected as immaterial, with LOW confidence.

label: PIONEEREMB
rationale: Size is unknown: the borrowing reduction is unquantified, and TTM revenue is Rs 198 cr. The profit gain is mainly the interest-cost effect of lower borrowings, a financial change, and the margin move has no identified operating event. Reject as a financial change with no operating explanation.

label: HAL
rationale: The 48,000 crore contract is a stated value (inclusive of taxes, period not stated), about 216% of TTM revenue of INR 22,255 crore; even a pre-tax value would stay far above 10%. It is firm, received for 83 aircraft, and called the biggest ever contract, so it is not routine. The MoUs carry no value. No disqualifier applies: the company is profitable and the customer is a defence programme, not internal demand.

label: MBECL
rationale: Firm LOA of INR 643.10 crore is about 139% of trailing revenue of INR 464 crore, but this is the JV total and MBECL's share is unstated. The order is not routine given no earlier comparable disclosure. The company is stressed, however: trailing PAT of INR -224 crore, trailing finance cost of about INR 80 crore, a market cap near INR 205 crore and very thin trading. The margin improvement is off a -89.7% base, and nothing shows the project will be profitable or funded, so it is not established that the order is the fix. Rejected as stressed; revisit if the JV share and funding plan are disclosed.

label: ACE
rationale: The forklift order is firm and company-specific, but at an estimated Rs 1.96 crore (28 units x assumed Rs 7 lakh) it is about 0.18% of trailing revenue of Rs 1,075 crore, so it is immaterial. The profit and finance-cost changes in the same results have no operating explanation in the packet and are not tied to this order. Rejected as immaterial, with the unexplained financial change noted for the record.

label: TARIL
rationale: Orders from a state utility and EPC contractors are the ordinary product flow for a transformer and rectifier maker, and the packet states no order value or quantity, so size against TTM revenue of INR 621 crore is unknown. The margin gain has no operating explanation beyond these routine orders, and TTM PAT is still slightly negative. Rejected as routine flow; LOW confidence because the packet has no earlier order history to test against.

label: INE999B01013
rationale: Frugal pre-filter (no model call): the packet has no order, commercial start, capacity or approval event, so under rules 3.3 it cannot be a pick; a financial change alone is not an inflection.

label: KPIL
rationale: The INR 1,554 crore award is firm and equals 12.5% of TTM revenue of 12,390 crore. It is routine: the company received 13,744 crore of orders in the nine months to Dec 2020, about 1,530 crore a month, so a 1,554 crore award is roughly one normal month's inflow and not a change in trajectory. No disqualifier is found, but the order is business as usual and is rejected.

label: ADANIGREEN
rationale: The 600 MW hybrid letter of award is firm and, at a 35% hybrid load factor and an assumed INR 2.5/kWh tariff, is worth about INR 460 crore or 16% of TTM revenue. It is routine, because the company already carries 11,820 MW awarded and under implementation and a 600 MW award is about 5% of that pipeline, so it is business as usual. The company is not stressed on TTM profit, but its high finance cost and equity raise are noted; the trigger is rejected as routine.

label: SUTLEJTEX
rationale: Size is an estimate from the stated 120 MT/day capacity at 50% year-one utilisation and an assumed INR 90/kg realisation, giving about 197 crore or 11.3% of TTM revenue of 1,743 crore. Commercial production has started, so the event is firm, and a recycled PSF plant is a new product line rather than business as usual. The company is loss-making on a TTM basis, but Q3 FY21 was profitable and the packet does not show a debt level that makes it stressed, so no disqualifier is applied; total debt and funding are unknown. Confidence is medium because the size rests on an assumed unit price.

label: AARTIIND
rationale: The 891 crore figure is an aggregate capex plan, not an operating event, and it is not firm and has no stated product or quantity to size. The gross margin rise and finance cost fall are financial changes with no operating explanation in the packet, and the margin was already in reported results. The margin trigger has been stale for over 200 days with no mechanism identified, so it is rejected.

label: BLS
rationale: The Embassy of Thailand contract is firm but its value is not disclosed, so its size against TTM revenue of 485 crore cannot be measured. The company itself describes it as its third embassy win in three months, so it is routine embassy and visa-services flow rather than a change in trajectory. No disqualifier is needed to reject it, and the 2021-02-03 margin change has no operating event in the packet to explain it.

label: GENCON
legal_name: Generic Engineering Construction and Projects Limited
rationale: The 80.80 crore order is firm and from an external counterparty, but size cannot be measured because no revenue is public by the cutoff. It is routine on this packet: a 41.37 crore order two weeks earlier and an outstanding order book of about 1,200 crore show the company wins orders of this size regularly. The 1,288.58 crore figure is the order book, not a new order.

label: SIEMENS
rationale: Frugal pre-filter (no model call): the packet has no order, commercial start, capacity or approval event, so under rules 3.3 it cannot be a pick; a financial change alone is not an inflection.

label: OLECTRA
rationale: The 350-bus letter of award to EVEY from an external state government undertaking is firm, and EVEY will procure the buses from Olectra, so this is treated as Olectra's own firm order with related-party execution risk. At an assumed INR 1.0 crore per bus the order is about INR 350 crore, roughly 172% of TTM revenue of 204 crore, and no comparable bus order appears in the packet, so it is not routine. The company has positive TTM PAT of 15.8 crore and falling finance cost, so no stressed-company disqualifier applies; the 300-bus tender is only L-1 and is not counted.

label: IOLCP
rationale: Size cannot be measured: the packet has no financials and no tonnage for the 30 percent Ethyl Acetate increase. The capacity and Gabapentin start are management plans, not commissioned capacity, so they are not firm. The debt-reduction item is contradicted by management and is financial in any case, so this is a watch until the expansion is commissioned and sized.

label: HIRECT
rationale: The two quantified orders are firm and total INR 111.27 crore, about 36% of TTM revenue of 307 crore, which clears the 10% threshold. The packet discloses no earlier orders, so nothing shows that orders of this size are routine, and the company is not stressed on the figures shown (small finance cost, positive TTM PAT). Confidence is low because the order history, execution period and margin are absent and the third order is unquantified.

label: GAIL
rationale: These are GAIL's own LNG purchase contracts, which are supply inputs and carry no revenue of their own, so no revenue-based size can be measured and the packet gives no volume-to-revenue link. The 376 bps gross margin rise covers the quarter ended December 2020, before the contracts were announced, so they cannot explain it. With no operating event that changes revenue, the margin move is a financial change with no operating explanation.

label: SOTL
rationale: Frugal pre-filter (no model call): the packet has no order, commercial start, capacity or approval event, so under rules 3.3 it cannot be a pick; a financial change alone is not an inflection.

label: LUMAXTECH
rationale: Commercial production at the Gurugram facility is firm, and a new facility and product lines would be non-routine, but the packet gives no revenue figures and no quantity, so size cannot be measured against annual revenue. The oxygen sensor order is only planned, and the commercial start was first disclosed in Sept 2020, so the event may already be partly in reported results. No disqualifier is found, so the company goes to watch until a quantified order or first results show the new revenue line.

label: BOROLTD
rationale: Frugal pre-filter (no model call): the packet has no order, commercial start, capacity or approval event, so under rules 3.3 it cannot be a pick; a financial change alone is not an inflection.

label: DCW
rationale: Frugal pre-filter (no model call): the packet has no order, commercial start, capacity or approval event, so under rules 3.3 it cannot be a pick; a financial change alone is not an inflection.

label: RAIN
rationale: No size can be measured: the forward price increase is unquantified, the reported EBITDA gains are already in results, and the 146 USD million item is capex spent in 2020, which never sizes an event. Management's statement that CPC and CTP prices will rise is credible and company-specific but not firm and may be cyclical, so it is a watch. The debt-reduction items are financial changes and do not qualify.

label: RAILTEL
rationale: The 25.46 crore per annum purchase order from BSNL is a received, firm order from an external customer and has no earlier comparable disclosure, so it is not routine on this packet. Size as a percent of revenue is unknown because no financials are public by the cutoff, so the 10 percent test cannot be applied and the most the packet supports is a watch. The milestone that would support deep research is commissioning and revenue disclosure under the order.

label: KUANTUM
rationale: Frugal pre-filter (no model call): the packet has no order, commercial start, capacity or approval event, so under rules 3.3 it cannot be a pick; a financial change alone is not an inflection.

label: HGINFRA
rationale: Frugal pre-filter (no model call): the packet has no order, commercial start, capacity or approval event, so under rules 3.3 it cannot be a pick; a financial change alone is not an inflection.

label: RITES
rationale: The INR 93 crore order is firm and equals 5.2% of TTM revenue of 1,794 crore, and the INR 61 crore HORC order adds about 3.4%, so the disclosed orders total under 10%. The company says it secured more than 60 projects or contracts in Q3 FY21 alone, so these orders are routine flow for a consultancy business, not an inflection. No disqualifier is applied; the rejection rests on routine flow and immateriality.

label: ADOR
rationale: Frugal pre-filter (no model call): the packet has no order, commercial start, capacity or approval event, so under rules 3.3 it cannot be a pick; a financial change alone is not an inflection.

label: THOMASCOOK
rationale: Frugal pre-filter (no model call): the packet has no order, commercial start, capacity or approval event, so under rules 3.3 it cannot be a pick; a financial change alone is not an inflection.

label: ADANIPORTS
legal_name: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited
rationale: The only operating item is an MoU with the Gujarat government described as exploring possibilities, with no value, area or timeline, so it is not firm and size cannot be measured. It is borderline and is a watch only because the new business is company-specific. The 500 crore INR debt-free item and the margin gains (already in reported results) are not operating events and do not qualify.

label: A2ZINFRA
rationale: Frugal pre-filter (no model call): the packet has no order, commercial start, capacity or approval event, so under rules 3.3 it cannot be a pick; a financial change alone is not an inflection.

label: ALICON
rationale: Order values are not disclosed and no financials are public by cutoff, so size against revenue is unknown. Per the concall the company books about INR 250 cr of new orders a quarter, and the Eaton and Eicher wins (a repeat/development order and an EV order on existing part lines) are part of that routine flow. The price increase is a raw-material pass-through, so this is not a change from business as usual.

label: INDOCO
rationale: Frugal pre-filter (no model call): the packet has no order, commercial start, capacity or approval event, so under rules 3.3 it cannot be a pick; a financial change alone is not an inflection.

label: SHALBY
rationale: The only operating event is a management statement of about INR 200 cr of capex for new hospital capacity. It is a plan, not firm, and capex does not size an event; no bed count or revenue quantity is in the packet, so size is unknown. The margin and finance-cost moves have no operating explanation and cannot support a pick. Watch until the expansion is approved and dated with a revenue quantity.

label: TALBROAUTO
